articles.body: WWE superstars have one of the largest fanbases in the world; however, a lot of fans have been known to cross personal boundaries on numerous occasions. These people have been known to be a danger to the superstars. A recent incident pertains to WWE legend Randy Orton, who had to deal with an obsessive fan that showed up on his doorstep.WWE star Randy Orton's fan showed up at his homeA video on social media showed a fan showing up at Randy Orton's home in hopes of getting an autograph. As he rang the doorbell, Randy Orton answered the door, and it led to a heated argument between the duo. Evidently, the 14-time WWE World Champion was not happy about a random person, even if it was a fan, showing up at his house unannounced. You can see the video of the encounter below:Randy Orton dealt with a similar fan encounter this yearRandy Orton is no stranger to such fan behavior. A few years ago, Orton was attacked by a fan who ran in the ring and low-blowed him before being nabbed by the security at a WWE live event. Moreover, before this home incident this year, Orton faced a similar situation during WrestleMania season. The Viper was mobbed by the fans as he was trying to get to an elevator at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas.Randy Orton is currently in a feud with Cody Rhodes on WWE televisionApart from the fan encounters, Randy Orton is currently embroiled in a feud with his former protege, Cody Rhodes. It began on the road to WrestleMania 42, where Orton turned on Rhodes and unleashed his most vicious side. Despite that, the Viper failed to beat the American Nightmare for the Undisputed WWE Championship in the main event of Night 1 of WrestleMania.Orton was absent from WWE television until SummerSlam 2026, where he made his shocking return and attacked Rhodes, reigniting their feud. This led to their rematch at Sunday Night's Main Event, which Orton won, despite Rhodes having the hometown advantage. Moreover, both men have continued their feud after their last match. articles.title: "It’s a shi**** feeling"- Former WWE star says company broke his "trust" after promising to help him secure acting opportunities
articles.summary: A former WWE star slammed the company for making false promises to him regarding potential acting opportunities.
articles.body: A former WWE star slammed the company for making false promises to him regarding potential acting opportunities. He is former NXT Champion Killer Kross, who was released from the company after SummerSlam 2025.Former WWE star Killer Kross made a huge WWE-TKO revelationIn an interview with The Wrestling Classic, Killer Kross said a company meeting stated that the merger to create TKO would bring more entertainment opportunities for WWE superstars. After that, Kross had approached WWE for those opportunities, citing his theatre background and personal interest.He said, “So I followed up afterwards once the meeting was done, and I said, ‘Hey, listen. I’m not looking to leave wrestling. I love wrestling. It’s my first passion. I don’t even know what life would be like without wrestling. But I would be interested in attempting to take on some, you know, different acting roles and stuff like that.’ I have a background in theater and such… I think… I could actually do some mainstream stuff in acting, and I could maybe create some new fans and bring them back into wrestling.”Killer Kross said that he was promised acting opportunitiesKiller Kross said that he was told to follow up with the WWE executives. However, nothing ever came to fruition despite him waiting for months. "I was told to follow up in October, and I’d be flown into Los Angeles and they’d introduce me to all these people and blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.And I followed up, and none of that ever happened. And then I waited a couple more months and I followed up, and none of that ever happened", said Kross.However, Kross made it clear that he could have reached out for those opportunities on his own. He didn't, as he was made to believe that WWE would help him, but they didn't, and Kross bluntly said that they broke his trust. "I said, ‘Well, I’m not dependent on this particular lead. I can pursue this on my own. I just wish that I wasn’t led to believe and told to do this. It’s a shi**** feeling, you know what I mean? Like, especially in a business that’s completely based on trust", said the former WWE star.Killer Kross has been wrestling for a lot of promotions on the independent circuit and pursuing other opportunities on his own now. articles.title: Asian Games: Birthday girl Lovlina Borgohain makes history with gold, joins Mary Kom in elite club
articles.summary: NEW DELHi: Birthday girl Lovlina Borgohain gave herself the perfect gift on Friday, scripting history by becoming only the second Indian woman boxer to
articles.body: NEW DELHi: Birthday girl Lovlina Borgohain gave herself the perfect gift on Friday, scripting history by becoming only the second Indian woman boxer to win an Asian Games gold medal after the legendary MC Mary Kom.The 29-year-old Indian defeated China's Ziyi Bao 5-0 in a closely contested women's 75kg final in Aichi-Nagoya to finally add the Asian Games gold to the silver she won at the previous edition.Lovlina's triumph also ended a wait that began in Hangzhou, where she had reached the final but lost to another Chinese boxer, Li Qian, to settle for silver.On Friday, however, there was no denying her.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleLovlina holds nerve in tight finalThe Indian made a confident start to the final, edging the opening round 3-2 on the judges' scorecards. Bao responded with an aggressive approach in the second, forcing Lovlina into a more defensive mode as the two boxers engaged in a series of exchanges in the middle of the ring.Despite the pressure, Lovlina remained composed and finished the round strongly. She won it 4-1 to stretch her overall advantage to 2-0 heading into the final round.With the gold within touching distance, Lovlina produced another controlled performance in the third. She again won the round 4-1 to complete a comprehensive 5-0 verdict and claim the biggest title of her Asian Games career.The victory was particularly significant given the quality of opposition she had overcome on her way to the final.In the semifinal, Lovlina edged reigning 70kg world champion Natalya Bogdanova of Kazakhstan 3-2 in another closely fought contest.From silver in Hangzhou to historic goldIn the semis, Lovlina had struggled to find her rhythm in the opening round against Bogdanova and went behind 2-3 on the judges' cards. She changed gears in the second, becoming more aggressive and landing cleaner punches to dominate the round 5-0.Bogdanova came forward again in the decider, while Lovlina relied on her defence and counter-attacks. The Kazakh edged the round 3-2, but Lovlina's advantage from the second round proved decisive.She secured the split-decision victory after three of the five judges scored the bout in her favour, booking her place in a second successive Asian Games final.That achievement had already made Lovlina the first Indian woman boxer to reach back-to-back Asian Games finals. Her gold on Friday now puts her alongside Mary Kom, who won the women's flyweight gold at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.India's boxing campaign has already surpassed its medal tally from Hangzhou. The country had won four medals at the 2023 edition, including one silver and three bronze. This time, Indian boxers have already secured six medals, with two more gold-medal opportunities remaining on Friday.Parveen Hooda will fight for gold in the 65kg category, while Ankush Panghal will contest the 80kg final later in the day.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: OTD (02/10/2021): Lee Johnson And His Fratton Park Fiasco!
articles.summary: Sunderland’s encouraging start to the season came crashing down in the rain at Portsmouth, as Lee Johnson’s young side were comprehensively beaten 4-0 at Fra...
articles.body:
Maybe I am wrong, but unless you are a southerner — or stone mad — an away day to Fratton Park is not one that stands out on the calendar. Sunderland's experiences down there over the years have not exactly been pleasant. I recall a defeat for Ricky Sbragia near the end of the season, when it was the first time I genuinely panicked that we were going to get relegated, along with Luke O'Nien's assault by a man of similar stature to Barney Gumble from The Simpsons , as two moments I would rather forget as a Sunderland fan.

The 2nd October is also one of those moments where, had it not been for researching this article today, I would have hoped never to think about it again for the rest of my life. I apologise for rehashing it.

It was an extremely wet and stormy day on the south coast, with conversations about whether the match should even go ahead becoming increasingly prominent as puddles began to form all over the pitch.

Lee Johnson's new-look side had started the season positively, losing just one of their first nine games before this fixture. Their opponents, Portsmouth, had not won in six, so there was plenty of reason for the 2,100 travelling Sunderland supporters to feel confident heading into a sodden afternoon on the south coast.

Within minutes, however, the conditions and the contest were turning ugly.

The rain continued to hammer down, the pitch became increasingly waterlogged and Sunderland looked completely out of their depth. Passes were going astray, challenges were being lost and Portsmouth seemed to have far more appetite for the battle. Every loose ball appeared to fall to a blue shirt and Sunderland were being bullied around the pitch.

This was a glimpse of a Lee Johnson team when they simply were not on it.

You could perhaps point towards the conditions as an excuse, but Portsmouth were playing in exactly the same weather. They were sharper, more aggressive and far more streetwise, while Sunderland struggled to cope with a game that had quickly descended into a physical scrap.

The opening goal felt inevitable when it eventually arrived. Marcus Harness put Portsmouth ahead before Lee Brown doubled their advantage, leaving Sunderland rocking in the relentless rain.

Things went from bad to worse before half-time when John Marquis added a third.

Three goals down at the break, Sunderland had been completely blown away in the first half and it didn't get much better in the second with the game finishing 4-0.

Johnson's young side looked incapable of dealing with the conditions or the physicality of their opponents, while Portsmouth had embraced the chaos. For the travelling supporters, drenched on the south coast and watching their team being comprehensively outplayed, it was becoming a miserable afternoon very quickly.

After the game, a visibly frustrated Lee Johnson tried to explain the reasons behind such a resounding defeat, whilst also apologising to the fans for such a bad day at the office.

"They just played the conditions better than us, simple as that," Johnson said.

"They had more bite in the tackle, they had energy and cohesion in the press, and our quality was poor.

"Conditions were tricky but we talked about that and about how it would be a test for our young team, and today we were found wanting completely.

"But it is one game, it's three points that hurts us because we felt it was one we could win.

"There's a lot of lessons for us to be learnt about those conditions.

"We're really appreciative of the crowd and their reaction at the end. It was incredible support in those conditions and to have travelled so far, we can only apologise."

In fairness to Johnson, he still had plenty of credit in the bank at this stage. Sunderland had made a positive start to the season and there had been plenty of genuinely exciting football along the way.

However, the excuses bank was going to expand with time, until eventually they were no longer acceptable.

Despite some genuinely exciting and fun football to watch, Johnson's side simply didn't seem to understand the concept of defending, nor did they display much of an appetite for it. That ultimately became the defining flaw of his Sunderland team — and, eventually, the reason he lost his job.

Fratton Park was a horrible afternoon, but perhaps it was also an early warning of what was to come.

articles.title: Igor Shesterkin Does Something No Rangers Goalie Has Ever Done
articles.summary: New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin joined some elite company on Thursday night, after doing something never seen before at MSG. The post Igor Sheste...
articles.body:
Igor Shesterkin pulled off something that no other New York Rangers goalie has ever done. And considering how long the team has been around, it's something truly remarkable.

On Thursday night, he finally added something nobody else in franchise history had managed to do.

The Rangers goaltender put the finishing touch on New York's 5-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning , firing the puck into an empty net as the Lightning pulled Andrei Vasilevskiy in an attempt to get back into the game.

It was the perfect punctuation mark on an otherwise outstanding performance.

Igor Shesterkin stopped 24 of 25 shots, helping the Rangers erase the disappointment of their 3-0 season-opening loss to Boston. The Rangers returned home for their first game at Madison Square Garden and immediately gave their star goaltender plenty of offensive support.

Then Shesterkin got in on the fun himself.

And that made the night considerably more memorable.

Shesterkin Finally Did What No Rangers Goalie Had Done

No Rangers goaltender had ever been credited with a goal before Thursday night.

That's remarkable considering the franchise dates back to 1926 and has employed some of the best puck-handling goaltenders in NHL history. Even Hall of Famer Ed Giacomin, one of the better puck-handlers of his era, never managed to score.

Igor Shesterkin had come agonizingly close several times.

He missed wide against Ottawa in 2022. He had another near-miss against Florida in 2023. And more recently, he nearly scored against Utah before the puck missed the net.

He even joked about how much he wanted to finally accomplish it at Madison Square Garden.

And considering how the goal happened, it was fitting.

Tampa Bay had pulled Vasilevskiy with the Lightning trying to mount an improbable comeback. Shesterkin got the puck, saw the empty net at the other end and made no mistake.

After the Rangers were shut out in Boston two nights earlier, their home opener couldn't have ended much better.

Igor Shesterkin didn't just make the saves.

Igor Shesterkin Joins a Very Exclusive Club

Goalie goals remain one of the rarest feats in hockey.

Before Shesterkin, only 15 goaltenders had been credited with a regular-season goal in NHL history. Minnesota's Filip Gustavsson became the 15th in October 2024 when he shot the puck into the empty net against St. Louis. It was also the third consecutive season in which an NHL goalie had scored by actually shooting the puck into an empty net.

The season before that, Pittsburgh's Tristan Jarry became the previous goalie to accomplish the feat.

Then there was Igor Shesterkin's fellow Russian and crosstown rival, Ilya Sorokin.

Sorokin was credited with his first career goal in March 2025 when Nashville's Steven Stamkos accidentally sent the puck into his own empty net after Sorokin was the last Islander to touch it.

And after years of near misses, he finally got his moment.

For a goaltender who had already won the Vezina Trophy, signed the biggest contract ever given to an NHL goalie and established himself as one of the league's elite netminders, there wasn't much left to add.

articles.title: Michael Pittman Jr. invisible once again in Week 4
articles.summary: Michael Pittman Jr. was held to two catches for 15 yards during the team's Week 4 matchup with the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers WR Michael Pittman Jr. caught two passes for 15 yards in a Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns . He was targeted four times.

Why It Matters: When the Steelers acquired Pittman and promptly inked him to a two-year extension, it seemed like they had big plans for the veteran wideout. On paper, he looked like a good fit as a sure-handed possession target that worked near the line of scrimmage with a quarterback that wants to get the ball out of his hands. Thus far, Pittman has just seven catches on the year and trails names like Roman Wilson and Darnell Washington in terms of receiving yards. It's still a bit premature to banish Pittman to waivers, but you can keep him parked on the bench until he shows more involvement in the offense.

articles.title: Wild rumors: Will Brock Faber’s busted face lead to nightmare Quinn Hughes trade scenario?
articles.summary: One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Minnesota Wild is the future of defenseman Quinn Hughes, whom they acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a blo...
articles.body:
One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Minnesota Wild is the future of defenseman Quinn Hughes , whom they acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a blockbuster trade last season.

Hughes is entering the final year of his contract, which carries a salary-cap hit of just under $8 million. His next deal is expected to be worth significantly more. However, the Wild recently faced a more immediate concern on the blue line when Brock Faber suffered a fractured skull blocking a shot against the Dallas Stars during the preseason. Faber underwent surgery and is out indefinitely.

Per NHL analysts Michael Russo and Joe Smith, Faber's injury could potentially have an effect on Hughes' long-term future with the club, considering their status as partners on the blue line.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"One of the reasons Hughes has loved playing in Minnesota was seeing how effective he could be playing alongside Faber," Russo and Smith wrote via The Athletic. "No defense pair logged more ice time together in the NHL after Hughes' arrival. No defense pair created more actual and expected goals."

"So not only could Faber's indefinite absence directly impact wins and losses this season, but it also could directly impact Hughes' mood. Suddenly he won't have his partner in crime around to shoulder the load. Suddenly, he'll have to carry the blue line — at least offensively — even more."

Hughes played 27:30 and had an assist with five shots on goal during Minnesota's 3-1 victory over the Nashville Predators at Bridgestone Arena on Thursday evening in their season-opener.

articles.title: Franco Colapinto handed extra grid penalty at F1 Bahrain GP
articles.summary: Off the back of his Baku penalty, Franco Colapinto is set for another grid penalty at Formula 1's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
articles.body:
Alpine driver Franco Colapinto is set for an additional grid penalty at Formula 1's Bahrain GP in Malaysia after taking a new Mercedes V6 engine.

Colapinto was set for a five-place grid drop at Sepang, which he carried over from last weekend as a punishment for causing a collision with Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris in Baku.

The Argentinian will now be demoted further for taking a fifth Mercedes internal combustion engine for the year, exceeding the annual allowance of four units.

It is understood that because Colapinto is already losing five places on the starting grid anyway, making a recovery to the points difficult, Alpine felt it was worth introducing a new Mercedes V6 here to minimise the damage. Colapinto will now receive an additional 10-place penalty, with a total of 15 places likely meaning a start on the back row.

Alpine is embroiled in a tight battle with Racing Bulls for fifth place in the constructors' championship, having been dealt a blow by Colapinto's Baku accident as Racing Bulls capitalised. Instead of gaining ground on Racing Bulls, Alpine's deficit grew to 15 points in the Azerbaijani capital.

Franco Colapinto, Alpine, Lando Norris, McLaren

Colapinto's team-mate Gasly is also due a new power unit over the next few races, but Alpine has not yet decided when it will introduce the new engine and take a grid penalty.

In Malaysia, Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad will also take a penalty for taking a new engine, turbocharger and exhaust, demoting him to the back of the grid, while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar goes back five places for taking his seventh V6 engine of the year.

articles.title: Classrooms created in former Everton stadium
articles.summary: New classrooms have been created at Everton's Goodison Park stadium in a bid to inspire learners.
articles.body:
New classrooms have been created at Everton's Goodison Park stadium in a bid to inspire young learners.

Everton Football Club has partnered with Everton Multi-Academy Trust to install the learning areas in the Park End stand, in former TV broadcast boxes.

The college classrooms have been designed with views of the pitch in an attempt to encourage children from disadvantaged backgrounds to attend school.

Former Everton midfielder Graham Stuart, who is also the club's ambassador, hoped it would inspire children.

"It must be great for the kids to be able to turn around and say, you know, where I go to school, Goodison Park," he said.

"Hopefully it is inspiring to the kids. One of the classrooms overlooks the pitch so I bet there's a clamour for the kids to be in that classroom."

The stand has been redeveloped inside to accommodate 250 Everton College students, some of which will sit in view of the pitch during lessons.

Others will learn in what used to be the hospitality area at Everton's original home.

The aim is to further link sport with education, getting more young people to attend school.

Connor Atkinson, who works for Everton in the Community having previously studied at Everton College, said he didn't take school seriously until he joined the college, and the lessons involved sport.

"I was a little bit disengaged and I didn't do the best in in in terms of GCSE results," he said.

"Linking sport and education is massive. Every child, every young person is different and every child and young person has a different learning style."

Steven Baker OBE, CEO of Everton Multi-Academy Trust, said it was about combining "the power of football and the Everton crest with our award-winning approach to education, helping all children to thrive".

Stuart added it was important to see how Goodison still serves people in the area despite the men's team moving away.

"Some people's concern was that once we went down to Hill Dickinson we'd forget all about L4 - but that certainly was never, ever going to happen," he said.

"Goodison Park, our original home, is still hugely important to us and the whole community."

articles.title: Where in the world has Tobias Altschäffl been? Now we know
articles.summary: One mystery solved.
articles.body:
Jamal Musiala was not able to play a part in Germany's 2-0 victory over Serbia, but the Bayern Munich star was still in attendance to watch his teammates in action.

Musiala was spotted in the stands alongside Tobias Altschäffl, a familiar name to anyone who follows German football closely. Altschäffl spent years working for Bild and Sport Bild, eventually serving as Bild's deputy football chief before his departure from the company on June 1, 2026.

One of the media outlet's most active and respected journalists, it seemed like an abrupt exit — but at least now we know why he disappeared. His exit from Bild came somewhat unexpectedly, making his subsequent appearance in Musiala's circle particularly interesting. Altschäffl has now resurfaced as part of Musiala's management and communications team, adding someone with extensive experience and contacts across German football media to the Bayern Munich star's inner circle. Recent reporting has specifically described him as a public relations expert and a new member of Musiala's team.

That makes the sight of Musiala and Altschäffl together at the Germany game more than just a casual moment in the stands. It offers a glimpse into the increasingly important off-field structure surrounding one of German football's biggest stars.

For now, Musiala's priority remains returning to full fitness and getting back on the pitch. But as his profile continues to grow, the people around him will play an increasingly significant role in managing his career, media presence, and commercial interests.

articles.title: Scott targets Euro 2028 place with England
articles.summary: Alex Scott says his aim is be part of England's midfield for the 2028 European Championship.
articles.body:
Alex Scott says his aim is be part of England's midfield for the 2028 European Championship.

England, along with Wales, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland, will host the tournament in two years time.

Bournemouth's Scott, 23, made his England debut on Tuesday when he came on as a second-half substitute in the 2-0 Nations League win over Czech Republic.

"For me now, it's just to keep myself in the squad as much as possible, keep performing for my club and put myself in the best position to get called up every window," Scott told BBC Radio Guernsey.

"Then push these boys that have been starting for the past few years and in tournaments for England.

"I mean, that's the ultimate dream, the Euros in two years now, a home Euros.

"So for me, everything will be put in and focused on that and trying to impress as much as I can whenever I come away and put myself in the best possible picture to be in that Euro squad."

The highly-rated Cherries midfielder had interest from clubs including Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea over the summer - but he looks set to stay on the south coast until at least the end of this season.

Scott knows breaking into England's midfield will not be easy, competing with players including Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson, but it is a challenge he is ready to take on.

"I've got quite a bit of work to do to get on their level," he said.

"I know Elliott pretty well from youth teams, we won the Euros together last year, and obviously Dec and Jude are two of the best players from England.

"So I'm learning off them and speaking to them as much as possible.

"They're great people as well, you can ask them about anything, they'll help with everything you need on the pitch and off the pitch.

"They're great human beings, so being here and around them, there's loads I can learn from them and what they've done and any advice they've got, of course, I'll take it on board."

'I'll forever be grateful for all the people back home'

Scott's debut was huge news in his native island of Guernsey.

Having struggled while being on Southampton's books as a 13-year-old, Scott returned to the Channel Island and made his men's debut as a 16-year-old in the Isthmian League for Guernsey FC.

It was not long before his talent was spotted and he joined Bristol City's academy before starring in the Championship for the Robins and earning a £25m move to Bournemouth in the summer of 2023.

He became the second player from Guernsey to win a senior England cap after Southampton great Matt Le Tissier.

Scott feels the support he got when he returned to Guernsey as a teenager was the reason he has developed into the footballer he is today.

"I think at the age I was, 13, 14, it's sometimes best to step away from it and go and enjoy time with your friends and family, because I missed out on probably five years of my childhood, flying away every weekend to play football," he said.

"When I went to Bristol City, I was in the under-18s there and I think I had a bit of a different experience and a different edge to some of the lads that were in that group, and that came from playing 14, 15 games of men's football with Guernsey FC.

"So that's definitely helped me along the way and the list would be endless if I could thank everyone.

"But I've had some amazing coaches and people around me that have helped non-stop from the age of 14 or 15 to now 23, so I'll forever be grateful for all the people back home."

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Taiwan’s gender-row boxer Lin Yu-ting wins gold medal
articles.summary: Lin bags her second Asian Games gold medal, three years on from her success in Hangzhou in the 57kg class.
articles.body:
Taiwan boxer Lin Yu-ting , the Olympic champion who found herself embroiled in a major gender row at Paris 2024, has won gold at the Asian Games.

Lin beat China’s Yang Chengyu 5-0 on Friday in the women’s 60kg (132lb) final in Nishio, Japan, giving her a second Asian Games gold after winning in the 57kg (126lb) class in Hangzhou, China, three years ago.

The 30-year-old was backed by a small pocket of vocal Taiwan supporters in the Nishio Gymnasium in Nishio, southeast of Nagoya.

Towering over her opponent, Lin used her superior reach to take control of the bout and had a clear advantage heading into the third and final round.

She held off a late assault from Yang to take gold, celebrating with the minimum of fuss.

Lin told the AFP news agency before the Games that she had considered retiring after the Paris Olympics but wanted to carry on fighting in part to defy those who questioned her eligibility.

Lin and Imane Khelif of Algeria were disqualified from the 2023 world championships by the International Boxing Association (IBA) after the organisation said they failed unspecified gender eligibility tests.

However, the International Olympic Committee allowed them to compete in Paris, saying they were victims of “a sudden and arbitrary decision” by the widely discredited IBA. Both went on to win gold.

The set ended level, with both teams taking one point as India and Korea moved to 1-1.Korea then produced a stunning start to the second set, hitting a perfect 30 from their opening three arrows. articles.title: Super League Grand Final 2026: Pundit predictions as Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity eye historic victory
articles.summary: The Sky Sports Rugby League pundits have made their calls on who they think win the Super League Grand Final in 2026; watch Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity in the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports from 5pm
articles.body:
Who will win the Super League Grand Final 2026?

It is so difficult to pick and it is very much a 50/50, but I will go with Warrington. After a pretty scrappy performance in the semi-final, I believe they'll be much improved for the final.

Why is this particular final so special?

The final is special because we have teams that finished third and fourth battling it out at Old Trafford. That has never been done before.

I think Matty Ashton will pick up the Rob Burrow award. I fancy him for a long-range try this week.

It feels special because this time of year we have always had one of the big guns in the final.

The Wakefield story feels special, Warrington's pain and remarkable 70-plus year wait can be put to bed. Two great stories, one new name on the trophy.

I think it will go to Wakefield's No 9 Tyson Smoothy.

I think this will be really close and there'll be plenty of nerves because neither club has won a Super League Grand Final.

It almost feels a shame one of them has to lose because seeing a new name on that trophy will be brilliant for the competition.

Warrington are battle-hardened after a proper scrap at Headingley while Wakefield must be bouncing after what I'd call the biggest upset in Super League play-off history, beating the League Leaders 33-6 in their own backyard.

Getting to Old Trafford is the reward, but once you're there nobody remembers the runner-up. There's no nice way of losing a Grand Final.

The obvious names for the Rob Burrow award are George Williams and Max Jowitt. Ben Currie will be right in the mix and don't rule out one of Wakefield's big boppers Caius Faatili or Caleb Hamlin-Uele causing some damage.

Josh Thewlis is another young man made for the big stage but I keep coming back to Jack Sinfield. Sometimes the biggest stage finds the youngest star. If I was putting a pound on anyone, my pound would be on Jack.

Playing at Old Trafford on the day his dad delivers the match ball as well... you couldn't write it. Although knowing the Sinfields, they probably could.

I know this will be a very closely-matched final, but I have a feeling Wakefield finish off their fairytale and become the sixth-ever Super League winner. Just two seasons ago they were in the Championship, and now they are in the biggest match of them all.

Their pack has been unbelievable in 2026 and I think that will prove the difference. They have put their side on the front foot and made the space for their backs to shine. If they win that battle like they have done so many times, then I expect party time in Wakefield on Sunday when they return!

Simply put, we have never quite had a final like this before. For the first time, there is no Wigan, Leeds or St Helens.

It is a seismic moment for the sport and the latest signal that clubs, with the right backing and motivation, can get to the top.

Warrington have been waiting 71 years for a trophy. Wakefield were relegated less than five years ago. These are two sides who know that history is on the line - one of them now needs to grasp it.

I love the story of it so I think Jack Sinfield wins. Imagine the scenes - Sir Kevin Sinfield delivers the match ball as his son plays in his first Grand Final and then he wins the trophy named after the person who has inspired his father to raise millions for the MND community.

Sport has a funny way of doing things that are too beautiful to be believable.

History is guaranteed. Wakefield Trinity will play in their first Grand Final, while Warrington will be hoping to win the Super League title for the first time.

It's being played on the same weekend as the NRL Grand Final, which I'm a huge fan of. Also, Sir Kevin Sinfield will complete his latest 7 in 7 challenge at Old Trafford before kick-off, presenting the match ball. Also, the fact his son Jack is part of the Wakefield team. Either Max Jowitt or George Williams will get the fairy tale. Daryl Powell against his old club. So many stories! I could go on.

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

The match will take place at 6pm, with coverage on Sky Sports from 5pm.

articles.title: Wakefield Trinity: Legends status up for grabs in first Grand Final occasion
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity's stars of yesteryear are remembered in sepia; the class of 2026 have the chance to add some colour with the chance of Grand Final glory.
articles.body:
There is a moment in the 1939 film 'The Wizard of Oz' where Dorothy swaps her monochrome world for glorious, eye-opening technicolour the minute she touches down in the Land of Oz.

The same could be said for the moment, should it happen, that Wakefield Trinity get their hands on the Super League trophy this Saturday after the Grand Final against Warrington Wolves.

Metaphorically of course, but the achievements of that great club are still currently only to be seen in those black and white hues and are ripe for a dash of colour.

Derek 'Rocky' Turner, Neil Fox MBE, Don Fox, Harold Poynton, Ken Rollin... all legends of the 1960s and an era when all the silverware found its way to WF1.

Belle Vue, or the DIY Kitchens Stadium as it is now known, has had its special nights since, such as the win to relegate rivals Castleford and secure safety at their expense in 2006.

Amid all the adrenaline and excitement, that was survival. Not success.

Yet, this season poses a different storyline. Wakefield can achieve. Wakefield can be winners. Title winners, for the first time since 1968.

It is a notion that boss Daryl Powell has tapped into, as winger Tom Johnstone explains.

"Daryl put a Powerpoint presentation on the screen, and said 'You could be legends of this club', and that was it," Johnstone told BBC Radio 5 live.

"He didn't really go any further into it, he just put a seed in the back of your mind and just gave you that little nugget.

"I've been at this club for so long now and if we can be the first ones to bring success back to this club we will go down in history forever, not just at Wakefield but everywhere.

"To be the sixth name on the trophy is just massive motivation."

Listen to commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Radio Merseyside, BBC Radio Leeds and BBC Sounds; watch highlights Saturday, 3 October from 23:00 BST on iPlayer and BBC Two on Sunday at 13:45 BST

Going back to the movie theme, Wakefield's resurrection over the past three seasons is almost too fanciful for Hollywood's scriptwriters, given the rapid ascent.

Owner Matt Ellis is without doubt the lead character, having come in as a fan but also an incredibly wealthy and successful kitchen magnate.

It has been more than just investment thrown at it; for example Ellis has been hands-on with the stadium renovation in terms of standards and finish on the back of the work of former custodians Michael Carter and John Minards who set the ball rolling.

He also has brought drive and vision, and it was he who was determined to bring Powell to the club as head coach almost immediately after taking control.

"Everything has changed from the top to the bottom," Johnstone added. "Rather than going into individual key details, the facilities have changed, the manner of the club, just the belief and the ambition of the club is probably the best one.

"We used to say a lot of things and say we wanted to compete but we had no chance of doing it at the time. Whereas now, it's an elite club. It's run so well.

"Anything you need, you've got it. Matt will provide absolutely anything. He just wants to see success. And the players we've signed and the team we've built, it just shows. It's just night and day."

Ellis and Powell has been a near-perfect partnership; with promotion back to Super League, Wembley success in the 1895 Cup, and back-to-back play-off appearances in Super League all culminating in this Old Trafford opportunity.

Powell had enjoyed success at Featherstone and Castleford before a stint at Warrington ended prematurely, and joining Wakefield has had a revitalising impact on both club and coach.

"I've been super-fortunate to get to a club that I've felt at home in straight away," Powell told BBC Sport. "Then when you feel that you can really get after your work and get the right kind of people in.

"Our coaching staff are second to none, they're unbelievable people and then get the right kind of players in, people first, players second but very good players because if you get the right people you know they're going to work hard to be the very best they can be.

"I feel like we've got all that mix right and the ownership is great which sets us up - we're just in a zone where we're all proud of each other and I know that's that's pretty special."

'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield one win from title

Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final

Super League: Superb Wakefield stun Wigan to reach first Grand final - as it happened

Powell has turned to familiar faces to fill those key roles; Michael Shenton - once his captain at Castleford, is now his trusted assistant while Ste Mills - another accolyte of yore is the brains behind the recruitment.

Aside from that, former Trinity player and modern day favourite Danny Kirmond is also on the staff while the experienced Stu Dickens also adds to the brains trust.

On the pitch, Powell has reunited with Jake Trueman, whose form in his time at Castleford put him in the international picture, and Mike McMeeken, who was part of the 2017 team at the Tigers who lost to Leeds in the Grand Final.

Front-rower McMeeken's authority and presence were a huge pick up for Trinity when he signed from Catalans as a statement signing on their top flight return, part of a powerful pack which highlights the best of Mills' talentspotting.

Bringing that power are Ky Rodwell from NRL side Parramatta, and ex-Cronulla reserve grader Caleb Hamlin-Uele - both signed while Trinity were still in the Championship.

Since getting up, Caius Faatili was brought in from Queensland Cup side Sunshine Coast Falcons in 2025 and was an immediate success with his raw-boned and aggressive style; lean, muscular Isaiah Vagana is rangy and athletic in the back-row, while Samoa international Jazz Tevaga has brought NRL experience and abrasive swagger to the squad.

"Daryl's really shown how good of a coach he is just how he's brought players in that probably may not have been picked up because of not being as well known," McMeeken told BBC Sport.

"For example Caius, not many clubs would have known about him but he's seen the potential in him and the good thing is, I think he's only about 23 or 24 so it's quite scary to see how far people like him can actually go."

Will 2026 finally be Warrington Wolves' year?

Quiz: Name every Super League Grand Finalist

Without a major football club in the city, Wakefield Trinity are the prime attraction for support, and all the attention and focus has been shone on them this week.

More than 30,000 tickets have been sold for Old Trafford at Trinity's end, nudging the expected attendance past 70,000 for a showpiece that guarantees a new name on the trophy for the second year running.

Finishing fourth earned them a home eliminator where Leigh were beaten impressively, but it was the dismantling of treble-chasing Wigan in the semi-final which really caught the eye and gave growing hope that Trinity could create a seismic Super League shock.

The Wakefield club that Johnstone started out at is almost a different beast more than a decade on, for the better, but the fanbase has remained the same - committed, loyal and vocal.

"It'd mean everything to us but I think it would mean more to them," Johnstone continued.

"They've always been proud of the club but there's not been too much to be proud of in the past 20 years so it'd be amazing for them, it'd be special.

"I got stopped on the way to school with my kids the other day by someone saying 'Come on Wakefield!' and it's just good to see the club and the city going that way.

"It can only be good for rugby league and Super League for us to be growing and performing and it's finally pay back for all the loyal fans that have been here throughout the years."

It is a long time between drinks, 1968. For Wakefield, the hope is it is champagne rather than shandy they are enjoying come the final hooter on Saturday.

Yet regardless of the result, there will be immense pride. Wakefield are back, and the key for everyone at the club now is to ensure they stay there.

Saturday could be the catalyst for that. Wakefield - Wizards of Old Trafford has a ring to it, or Wizards of OT you might say.

articles.title: ‘I wanted to quit boxing’: Lovlina Borgohain fights through tough year to script historic Asian Games gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A year after questioning her future in boxing, Lovlina Borgohain found the perfect answer on Friday, winning Asian Games gold on her 29th
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A year after questioning her future in boxing, Lovlina Borgohain found the perfect answer on Friday, winning Asian Games gold on her 29th birthday.The 29-year-old had contemplated walking away from boxing after returning empty-handed from the Paris Olympics. Two years later, after enduring a difficult phase and questioning her future in the sport, Lovlina stood on top of the podium at the Asian Games — becoming only the second Indian woman boxer after the legendary MC Mary Kom to win the continental gold.“I wanted to quit boxing. But I continued. I had to change the colour of my medal. It was very important. More important than that is that I continued,” Lovlina said after defeating China's Ziyi Bao 5-0 in the women's 75kg final.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleFrom Paris heartbreak to Asiad gloryLovlina had won an Olympic bronze at Tokyo 2020 but returned from Paris without a medal. She subsequently took a year-long break before making her return to international boxing.The comeback, however, was far from smooth. She exited the World Championships in the second round and later skipped the World Boxing Cup final. At the Commonwealth Games this year, she had to settle for silver — a result that left her dissatisfied.“It was a tough year for me,” she said. “I was not happy about winning the silver medal at the Commonwealth Games. But, there are a lot of things in an athlete's life: losses, injuries. You have to handle a lot of things. This gold medal was very important to me.”The gold in Japan completed a remarkable turnaround for the boxer from Assam, who had won silver at the previous Asian Games after losing to China's Li Qian.‘I am feeling very good’Lovlina held her nerve in a closely fought final against Bao. She edged the opening round 3-2 on the judges' scorecards before winning the second 4-1. She maintained her composure in the final round to secure another 4-1 verdict and complete a 5-0 victory.The triumph ended India's 12-year wait for a women's Asian Games boxing champion, with Mary Kom having won flyweight gold at the 2014 edition in Incheon.Lovlina, however, was still taking in the magnitude of her achievement.“That is how I continued. I am feeling good. I don't know how to celebrate my gold. It has just ended. I need some time to accept that I have won. I am feeling very good.”‘You are confident, you are the best’Lovlina said the journey had also been about overcoming self-doubt. Looking back at her younger self, she said she would remind herself of the ability she possessed.“I had no confidence at that time, so if I had the chance to talk to my younger self I would tell her, 'You are confident, you are the best'. Now, I have a medal in every competition.”Mental strength, she added, was crucial when facing high-quality opponents.“I think it is important to be mentally strong. If we think that we have to win, no one can defeat us.”Japan, meanwhile, has now delivered another major moment in Lovlina's career.“I have to be strong and win. I was very positive about everything. Japan is very lucky for me. I was always think about winning.”And when asked whom she would call first after winning the biggest title of her Asian Games career, there was little hesitation.“The first person I am going to call is my mum. articles.standfirst: El extremo del Barcelona podría marcar en tres partidos consecutivos con España por primera vez desde su debut en 2023
articles.summary: El extremo del Barcelona podría marcar en tres partidos consecutivos con España por primera vez desde su debut en 2023
articles.body: Lamine Yamal ha arrancado la temporada de forma estelar. No sólo con el Barcelona, sino también con la Selección, donde está deslumbrando en estos primeros partidos de la Nations League. Ante la República Checa de Santi Denia, que conoce perfectamente al extremo desde sus etapas en las categorías inferiores, tendrá la oportunidad de tachar de su lista un hito que todavía no ha conseguido desde su debut con España en 2023: marcar en tres partidos consecutivos. La secuencia no puede ser más prometedora. Lamine viene de marcar contra Inglaterra en Wembley y de hacerlo por partida doble frente a Croacia en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. Dos actuaciones que han vuelto a confirmar su condición de futbolista diferencial y que le permiten presentarse ante Chequia con la posibilidad de prolongar su racha goleadora. Casino Gran Madrid paga a 1.95 que el atacante del Barcelona vuelva a ver puerta y consiga completar esa particular trilogía. Del grado de inspiración de Lamine dependerán buena parte de las opciones de España para sacar adelante un partido que puede dejar prácticamente sentenciado el pase a los cuartos de final de la Nations League como líder del grupo. La Selección llega con pleno de victorias y unas sensaciones inmejorables, mientras que el joven extremo se ha convertido en uno de los grandes argumentos ofensivos de Luis de la Fuente. Las apuestas deportivas de Casino Gran Madrid reflejan, además, un favoritismo abrumador para el conjunto español. La victoria de España se paga a 1.07, mientras que el empate alcanza una cuota de 10.0 y un triunfo de República Checa se dispara hasta los 31.0. Unas cifras que dejan claro el escenario que se espera en este tercer partido de la fase de grupos. Las mejores casas de apuestas también siguen de cerca la evolución de un Lamine que, con apenas 19 años, ya empieza a convertir cada partido con la Selección en una oportunidad para seguir ampliando sus registros. Porque el reto ante Chequia no será uno más para el extremo azulgrana. Después de marcar en Wembley y firmar un doblete ante Croacia, Lamine está a sólo un gol de conseguir por primera vez tres partidos consecutivos viendo portería con España. Casino Gran Madrid cotiza ese tanto a 1.95 y pone precio a una marca que todavía no figura en el historial de uno de los grandes protagonistas de esta nueva generación. El siguiente capítulo, ante un viejo conocido como Santi Denia.

articles.title: Manchester City to launch appeal as financial breach fallout grows
articles.summary: Friday deadline looms as the legal fallout widens beyond the Premier League case over the alleged breaches.
articles.body:
Manchester City are expected to press ahead with an ⁠appeal against ⁠findings that they breached Premier League financial rules by Friday’s deadline, opening a new chapter in a case that ⁠has already become one of the most significant in English football.

The club has consistently denied wrongdoing and indicated they will challenge an ⁠independent commission’s findings that they used “sham” commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19bn) over nearly a decade.

City have said they have a body of “irrefutable evidence” ‌that will clear the club’s name and are expected to argue that the government of Abu Dhabi – not the club’s owners – partly funded the sponsorship deals.

The Premier League’s new fast-track rules state that an appeal hearing must be held within 12 weeks of an appeal being lodged with a decision due within 30 days ⁠of the hearing concluding.

City are expected ⁠to argue the rules were not in place when they were originally charged in February 2023.

The breadth of the fallout facing Manchester City extends well beyond football sanctions.

On ⁠Thursday, the head of the Treasury Select Committee in the House of Commons asked Britain’s tax authority, His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC), what action it was ⁠taking in response to the Premier League’s findings.

Meg ⁠Hillier said she had written to HMRC Permanent Secretary JP Marks after the publication on Tuesday of the independent commission’s ruling that the club had committed “well over 100 ‌individual breaches of the Premier League rules across the course of many seasons”.

Sports lawyers have predicted years of further litigation as rival ‌clubs, ‌players and agents assess whether they may have grounds to pursue compensation claims connected to the case.

articles.title: Ranking the Top 10 NCAA Men's Hockey Players at the Start of the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: A new season of college hockey kicks off Friday night, but who has made the cut for our top players to watch this year?
articles.body:
A new season of college hockey kicks off Friday night, but who has made the cut for our top players to watch this year?

With the NCAA becoming an increasingly attractive development route for players coming out of CHL major-junior hockey, college hockey has attracted more top-end talent than ever before.

NCAA rosters now feature players at vastly different stages of development: top-five NHL draft picks beginning their college careers at 18 alongside undrafted 23-year-olds still chasing a professional opportunity—and, in some cases, earning one.

Honorable mentions who just missed the cut but should still make noise this season include Tynan Lawrence (STL), Ethan Belchetz (UTA) and Ryan Lin (SJS).

Boston Bruins prospect and Boston College Eagles center Dean Letourneau has shown significant growth since he was drafted 25th overall in 2024. We expect him to take a further step this season.

Letourneau, drafted out of prep school, was already a good skater when he arrived in college. He was not merely a good skater for his size—he now stands 6'7" and weighs 229 pounds—but a legitimately good skater, period.

He combines that mobility with legitimate offensive skill. Although it took time for that skill to translate to the NCAA level, it became evident last season: Letourneau improved from three points in 36 games as a freshman to 39 points in 36 games last year.

Part of that improvement stemmed from increased opportunity—particularly on the power play, where he is especially effective. A larger factor, though, was Letourneau becoming more comfortable in the college environment and more confident in his own skill set.

He appears to be developing into a top prospect, and it will be intriguing to see what kind of step he takes this season.

9. Keaton Verhoeff, D, University of North Dakota

A 2026 draft pick, Keaton Verhoeff is going into his second season in the NCAA.

He was selected ninth overall by the San Jose Sharks from the University of North Dakota Fighting Hawks.

Verhoeff made an ambitious move from the WHL's Victoria Royals to North Dakota at age 17, entering an unfamiliar league for his draft-eligible season. The decision gave him an early NCAA test and could position him for a larger role—and a potential breakout—in 2026-27.

The defenseman combines excellent size and physicality with a high-end hockey IQ, tools he should be better positioned to maximize after adjusting to the college game.

His first season at North Dakota was promising, though he did not always look like the player who had stood out with the Victoria Royals a year earlier. At times, his highly regarded skating appeared stiff or clunky, and he occasionally misread plays that he may have handled more consistently in the WHL.

Verhoeff should be better equipped to avoid those growing pains this season after gaining a full year of NCAA experience. That year also included an underage appearance for Canada at the World Junior Championship, and he could be in line for a larger role at this winter's tournament.

Center Caleb Malhotra may be better known to some as the 3rd overall pick in the 2026 draft, or as retired NHLer (and current Vancouver Canucks head coach) Manny Malhotra's son.

But he is his own man, and his own player, and it is going to be so exciting to watch the college hockey audience witness his play week after week.

Malhotra is going to be a phenomenal NHL player—in the case of longevity and impact—which is why it's an excellent thing that he's taking time to develop and sand off the rough edges of his game in the NCAA first.

Last season saw Malhotra playing with the Brantford Bulldogs of the OHL, where, going into the season, he was highly touted for his defensive play and detail game. He rose sharply up the draft boards across the season as he made it increasingly clear that he was also a scoring and playmaking threat.

You can trust him anywhere on the ice, and he's able to drive play thanks to his excellent hockey sense. All of this bodes well for his transition to the NCAA game.

Staff Predictions for Stanley Cup Winner 🔮

7. Max Plante, C, University of Minnesota Duluth

Max Plante, the reigning Hobey Baker Award winner, is the first recipient to return to NCAA hockey for the following season rather than turn professional since North Dakota's Ryan Duncan did so in 2007.

Plante's decision was not driven by a lack of professional options, though.

The Detroit Red Wings, who drafted him in the second round in 2024, would probably be delighted to have him either in their fold or playing with their AHL affiliate the Grand Rapids Griffins.

Plante chose to return to the University of Minnesota Duluth because it gave him the opportunity to play with his brothers: Zam, a 2022 draft selection of the Pittsburgh Penguins, and Victor, a 2026 selection of the Detroit Red Wings.

He has also been recently afforded another fascinating opportunity. Having spent the last two winters representing the USA at the World Junior Championships, in this first year of him aging out of the tournament he's been named to the roster for the US Collegiate Selects, a team that represents the USA and NCAA hockey at the Spengler Cup.

Winning another Hobey Baker isn't out of the question either.

6. Wyatt Cullen, F, University of Minnesota

Unlike his peers, Wyatt Cullen is listed simply as a forward. That is not because his position is unclear, but because he has played both center and wing and has the tools to contribute at either spot.

It will be interesting to see where he settles under Brett Larson at the University of Minnesota.

Cullen—the son of former NHLer Matt—was drafted out of the USNTDP this year at 10th overall by the Nashville Predators. His draft position was the product of a roller-coaster season that began with a torn hip flexor, contributed to by a significant growth spurt and leading to a slow start, and ended with scouts agreeing that he was one of the best offensive talents available last year.

He was one of the youngest players in the 2026 draft class as well, just turning 18 this September.

Cullen is a creative and dynamic offensive player, with elite intelligence and playmaking abilities. He needs to add a layer of physicality to his game and some more muscle to his frame, but college hockey happens to be the perfect place for both of those things.

5. Michael Hage, C, University of Michigan

Montreal Canadiens prospect Michael Hage surprised everyone—including the Habs—when he decided to return to the University of Michigan for a third season.

That typically doesn't happen for top prospects drafted out of college hockey and Hage, a product of the development machine that is the Chicago Steel of the USHL, is definitely a top prospect.

When you take a moment and think about it, though, it makes sense. The Wolverines made it to the Frozen Four last year, and he had a taste of a potential championship only to have it taken away when they lost out on a finals berth. Going back for redemption is understandable.

Hage, a center, had 52 points in 39 games last season on top of 15 points in seven World Juniors games. We're likely going to see those offensive totals jump again (though he aged out of the WJC).

He's a fantastic puck-carrier, with terrific offensive instincts, and he understands how and when to create space for both himself and also his teammates through his playmaking. He's another one who definitely has Hobey Baker potential.

4. Carson Carels, D, University of North Dakota

Selected sixth overall in the 2026 draft by the Calgary Flames, Carson Carels is one of the players we are most excited to see in college hockey this season.

One of the hallmarks of his game is the fact that he likes to play mean, and does it well. That is going to serve him well in college hockey, which is often a more physical game than junior hockey.

Carels played with fellow North Dakota defenseman Keaton Verhoeff at last year's World Junior Championships, where they helped Canada to a bronze medal. Expect to see both of them back this season and playing a more significant role, with several players from that roster aging out.

Carels comes to North Dakota from the Prince George Cougars of the WHL, and please don't make the mistake of thinking that hallmark meanness is the only thing that he brings to the team. He's equally terrific at both ends of the ice, showcasing terrific skating skills and landing sneaky passes to teammates as easily as he lands heavy hits on opponents.

3. Landon DuPont, D, University of Michigan

We've reached an exciting unknown (as far as how he'll fare in college hockey goes; he's very known overall) quantity: projected top 2027 draft pick Landon DuPont.

Well, current projected top pick; we've seen what can happen across a season, and the transition to college hockey can trip up even the best of players. But we're not particularly worried about DuPont.

He joins the Wolverines from the Everett Silvertips of the WHL. He was a key piece of their WHL championship win and push for a Memorial Cup championship last season, and he will bring that intensity to the NCAA.

You may see detractors mention that he's 5'11", but ignore it. His play speaks for itself, as does his ability to absorb heavy and difficult minutes.

We've already provided an early scouting report but here's a quick rundown. DuPont is an excellent, speedy skater whose intelligence and creativity allow him to create and find teammates, and whose endless tenacity underpins it all.

It wouldn't be surprising to see the Wolverines use him on either the power play or the penalty kill, as he's been known to eat up minutes on both.

2. Chase Reid, D, Michigan State University

Defenseman Chase Reid was drafted seventh overall by the Seattle Kraken in June. Before that he was one of our top prospects for 2026.

His elite skill level is such that he could easily have been a top pick in another draft year—one without Gavin McKenna and with general managers less wary of selecting a somewhat slight player whose hockey intelligence surpasses that of nearly everyone else in his class.

Reid is incredibly offense-focused, but it's not to the detriment of his team or the rest of his game; it's in the way that the game moves through him when he is on the ice. He's able to control the flow and pace of the game when he has the puck, a true play driver and incredible puck carrier. His elite skating and hockey sense drive all of it.

He comes to the NCAA from the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the OHL, where he was a greater than point-per-game player despite being limited by injury. His school of choice was Michigan State University, a place that has done an excellent job securing commitments from top NHL-drafted prospects and should be a team to watch this season.

1. Ethan Wyttenbach, LW/RW, Quinnipiac University

Winger Ethan Wyttenbach was selected in the fifth round in 2025 by the Calgary Flames and is our top NCAA player to watch this season.

Returning to Quinnipiac University after a freshman season where he blew everyone away with his growth from the season prior, he has showcased a significant amount of growth since being drafted.

He earned the 2026 Tim Taylor Award, given to the best freshman D1 hockey player each year, and led the nation in points with 59 (25 goals and 34 assists). He was also named ECAC rookie of the year.

Wyttenbach is already being discussed as an early Hobey Baker Award candidate. His exceptional hockey IQ was a major factor in his impressive offensive production as a freshman, and it would not be surprising to see him take another step forward statistically this season.

He excels at creating time, space and passing options for teammates and is a true play driver because of his ability to read the ice.

Add to that his heavy shot and endless tenacity, and you have a recipe for a player the Calgary Flames are chomping at the bit to sign when his college season ends next spring.

articles.title: 2026 Asian Games: China's Tang Jing disqualified after alleged bite in bout with Rin Maeda
articles.summary: Chinese judoka Tang Jing is disqualified from the quarter-finals of the Asian Games with the coach of her opponent claiming that her athlete was left with bite marks on her arm.
articles.body:
Chinese judoka Tang Jing was disqualified from the quarter-finals of the Asian Games after appearing to bite the arm of Japanese opponent Rin Maeda.

Tang was disqualified for unsportsmanlike behaviour in the women's -70kg bout in Nagoya, with Maeda progressing and ultimately winning the event.

Having been separated from a hold early in the encounter, Maeda rolled-up her sleeve to show the referee her left forearm, with what appeared to be a bite mark visible just above the wrist.

Officials reviewed video footage before handing three-time Asian Games medallist Tang the disqualification.

"It looked like it was really going to bleed," said Maeda's coach Maki Tsukada.

"We didn't talk about disinfecting it or anything like that, but the bite mark was very clear and distinct."

Tang, 31, appeared to contest the decision before shaking hands with Maeda and leaving the competition area without offering the media interviews.

Maeda, 21, said she was unsure what would happen after she spoke to the referee.

"It's not something that happens very often, so it was a first for me," she told reporters after securing a gold medal with a victory over Kazakhstan's Azhar Askhat.

"I wasn't really sure what would happen myself, but I did tell the referee. I was in a little pain, but once I got on the mat, the adrenaline kicked in and I didn't really notice it, so it was fine."

articles.title: Ben Cabango: Haaland 'gave me his shirt, but he didn't take mine'
articles.summary: Ben Cabango will always have a memento to remind him of Wales' memorable victory over Norway – Erling Haaland's shirt.
articles.body:
Defender Ben Cabango will always have a memento to remind him of Wales' memorable victory over Norway – Erling Haaland's shirt.

Wales beat the World Cup quarter-finalists 2-1 in the Nations League with Cabango producing an outstanding display to keep Manchester City striker Haaland quiet.

The Swansea City defender revealed he asked Haaland for his shirt after the final whistle at the Cardiff City Stadium.

"I did grab it after the game," Cabango said.

"He was just there, so I thought, 'Why not?' He just gave me the shirt... but he didn't take mine."

Cabango was recalled to Wales' starting line-up following Sunday's 2-0 defeat against Denmark in Copenhagen.

The 26-year-old had played in the opening Nations League game against Portugal in Lisbon, where he faced Cristiano Ronaldo.

"It is surreal to play against Ronaldo and Haaland in the same camp," Cabango reflected.

"But it's definitely where you want to be, stay around that for as long as possible.

"You learn a lot playing against these players.

"You've got to be concentrated throughout the game and you can't switch off at any moment. That probably brings out the best side of me and it's been good."

Was long-awaited win a turning point for Bellamy?

Bellamy responds to abuse as Norway win lifts mood

Goals from Dan James and Neco Williams – after Oscar Bobb had given Norway an early lead – secured Wales' first win in seven games.

Cabango earned his 18th senior cap in what was also Wales' first ever win in Nations League A.

"I'd probably say it was my best game for Wales," Cabango added.

"I enjoyed the game, it was a good battle and we came out on top.

"I enjoy that side of the game. The ball's there to be won and I'm going to try and win it 100 per cent of the time and today it paid off.

"We needed to bounce back from the last game and I felt we all did that as a collective. All the squad, the players that came on, it was a real good performance."

Head coach Craig Bellamy praised the performance of Cabango and his defensive partner – captain Ben Davies – in subduing Haaland and Norway's forwards.

"They were brilliant – really, really good," Bellamy said.

"But the key part of that, which we mentioned before [the game] and the work we had done, was to keep them away from our box.

"It's easier said than done but that's why we were constantly pushing, constantly working to keep them as far away as we can.

articles.title: WWE's Royce Keys Has Arrived and The Bloodline Should Be Worried
articles.summary: Royce Keys and his new stable have emerged recently as a major threat to The Bloodline, and no one is safe.
articles.body:
Royce Keys and his new stable have emerged recently as a major threat to The Bloodline, and no one is safe.

The leader of The 946 has recruited two heavy hitters and used the element of surprise to beat Jacob Fatu and The Usos at their own game. While The Bloodline has dominated Raw and SmackDown, this is the most vulnerable the group has ever looked.

Pro wrestling stables have been a fixture on WWE programming during the Triple H era. For the last four years, the company has developed teams such as Damage CTRL, The Judgment Day and The Vision, particularly in the build to Survivor Series.

The 946 is the latest stable to run roughshod on Monday nights ahead of the 2026 men's WarGames match. It isn't a new approach, but it's a tremendous use of the powerhouse from East Palo Alto, California.

Keys has capitalized on his screen time as a standout in the main event segments of WWE's flagship series. His current push is a far cry from the uncertainty surrounding his start with the company.

In January, he left All Elite Wrestling and debuted as entrant No. 14 in the men's Royal Rumble match. Keys eliminated Damian Priest, a former world champion, proving he belonged on the big stage.

However, the timing of his arrival wasn't ideal because he didn't factor into plans for WrestleMania 42. This meant the new signee would have to wait a few months to start a noteworthy storyline with Fatu.

Keys' patience was ultimately rewarded as their brutal Street Fight led to his return with OTM, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price, to close the Aug. 24 episode of Raw. The new trio made a statement, taking out everyone in the ring, including his former allies, LA Knight and Solo Sikoa.

Since its debut, The 946 has become the brand's most dangerous and unpredictable stable, with a penchant for violence and wanton destruction. The latest member, Jaida Parker, even used a car to attack Fatu on national television this week.

The 946's introduction works so well because we've seen so many protagonists respond rationally to The Bloodline's repeated attacks. Roman Reigns finally pushed the wrong man over the edge, and the consequences have been swift.

Keys isn't trying to reason with them or trying to appeal to Raw general manager Adam Pearce. He has taken action into his own hands and exacted revenge on anyone who didn't help him.

Unlike Cody Rhodes or many others, the newcomer isn't trying to take Reigns' title to remove his hold on Raw.

Instead, Keys has sought to decimate and humiliate his opponents at every turn. The 946 is more vicious than any other opposition The Bloodline has faced because it's willing to take a scorched-earth approach.

This could play into the outcome of Reigns' upcoming World Heavyweight Championship match at Money in the Bank. WWE has put a lot of effort into legitimizing Keys and his stable as a volatile group, similar to fan favorites from The Attitude Era.

It's the over-the-top backstage drama that the company is known for, and it's great to see a fresh face in the mix. It took some time, but Keys has emerged as a significant figure with a clear plan of attack.

The Bay Area native is no longer the muscle in someone else's crew. He's the leader, and he's coming for everything. Everyone should be worried about what he will do to prove it in a WarGames match.

articles.title: India vs Pakistan cricket: Asian Games gold medal final – all to know
articles.summary: For the first time this year, archrivals India and Pakistan meet in a final, as they face off at the Asian Games.
articles.body:
Who : India vs Pakistan What : Asian Games 2026, men’s cricket final gold medal match Where : Korogi Athletic Park, Nisshin, Japan When : Saturday, October 3, 1:30pm local (04:30 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 02:30 GMT.

Cricket’s biggest rivalry will be renewed this weekend as India take on Pakistan in the Asian Games men’s cricket final, with the elusive gold medal at stake.

Saturday’s blockbuster clash, played in the Twenty20 format, will be held at Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi Prefecture, Japan.

India will defend their Hangzhou 2023 title, while Pakistan eye their first gold, having won bronze at Guangzhou 2010.

India’s Men in Blue can complete a cricket double in Aichi-Nagoya after the Indian women’s team clinched gold at the start of the Games, thrashing Sri Lanka in the final.

Al Jazeera tells you everything to know about India vs Pakistan:

What happened the last time India played Pakistan?

India and Pakistan last met in a T20 World Cup group-stage match in Colombo, Sri Lanka, on February 15.

India won that match by 61 runs , with Ishan Kishan’s 77 off 40 guiding them to victory.

The last time Pakistan defeated India in T20Is dates back to September 4, 2022.

Pakistan beat India by five wickets in that Asia Cup semifinal, as Mohammad Rizwan top-scored with 71.

How did India and Pakistan reach the Asian Games cricket final?

As two of the four seeded teams, both India and Pakistan directly qualified for the quarterfinals at the Asian Games 2026.

India’s quarterfinal against Afghanistan was abandoned due to rain, and World No 1 India proceeded to the semifinals due to their higher seeding, determined by the ICC T20I team rankings.

In the semis, India thrashed Sri Lanka by 124 runs , dismissing their opponents for 45 in 9.5 overs.

As for Pakistan, their quarterfinal tie with Hong Kong, China was also washed out, and they advanced to the semifinals in the same fashion.

World No 6 Pakistan clinched a six-wicket win over Bangladesh in their semifinal clash, which was reduced to 13 overs due to a wet outfield.

What happens if the India vs Pakistan final is washed out?

Rain has disrupted much of the cricket competition in Aichi-Nagoya.

If Saturday’s final is abandoned due to rain, India and Pakistan will share the gold medal.

This is different from what happened at Hangzhou 2023 – India were awarded the gold due to higher ranking after their last edition’s final with Afghanistan was washed out.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Ishan Kishan (India) : India’s 15-year-old batting prodigy Sooryavanshi is undoubtedly one of the best players to watch out for across all sports at the ongoing games. The big-hitting opener scored 38 runs in the semifinals, smashing six fours and two sixes. Middle-order batter Kishan’s unbeaten 80 off 46 balls was, however, the highlight of that match, with his incredible five sixes adding extra entertainment.

Sufyan Moqim and Abdul Samad (Pakistan): Left-arm wrist-spin bowler Moqim was the pick of Pakistani bowlers in their semifinal victory, bagging three wickets by conceding 26 runs in three overs. Samad, on the other hand, dazzled with the bat, scoring a quickfire, unbeaten 30 off 15 balls, smashing five fours and a six.

A day after returning home to Sangatpura village in Jind, the 27-year-old was asked to make another trip to Japan - this time to carry the Indian flag at the closing ceremony.The call came from former Indian shooter and India’s deputy chef de mission at Aichi-Nagoya Anjali Bhagwat, who told Neeru that she had been chosen as India's women's flag bearer for the closing ceremony of the Asian Games 2026.Neeru had returned to India only a day earlier after completing a memorable campaign in Aichi-Nagoya. She was still recovering from viral fever and feeling weak, but did not want to let the opportunity go.Within hours, she packed her bags and headed back to the airport."I am at the airport. The flight is in the next hour. I got a call from Anjali Bhagwat ma'am. She has asked me to be the flag bearer in the closing ceremony. It's a big honour for me. I didn't want to let it go," Neeru told TimesofIndia.com."My parents are so happy. When I gave them the news about the closing ceremony, my mother said, 'Ja beta, mauka nahi milta ye kisi ko. Aaja, fir se khushi manayenge,'" Neeru said.Asian Games Full Coverage|Medal Tally|ScheduleThe 27-year-old will fly back to Nagoya on Saturday and carry the Indian flag at the closing ceremony on Sunday.Neeru finished the Games with two gold medals and a silver, emerging as one of India's standout performers. She first won the women's individual trap gold before combining with Manisha Keer and Aashima Ahlawat to win silver in the women's trap team event.On the penultimate day of the shooting competition, Neeru partnered Kynan Chenai to win gold in the trap mixed team event. Her medal tally stood at three - two golds and a silver.The achievement came after a difficult few weeks for Neeru. Just before the Asian Games 2026, she suffered from viral fever and had to be admitted to PSRI Hospital in Chirag Delhi after her condition did not improve.Even after being discharged, she was still weak. But she travelled to Japan, competed, and returned with three medals.Now, despite still recovering from the illness, Neeru is making another trip to Japan. This time, she will lead the Indian contingent as the country's women's flag bearer at the Asian Games 2026 closing ceremony.Earlier this year, Neeru had also won the women's trap gold at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Furbank to make first start for Quins in Prem
articles.summary: George Furbank will make his first Prem start for Harlequins this weekend plus team news from all five games.
articles.body:
As we prepare for week two in the 2026-27 Prem season it feels like we are still getting warmed up for the new campaign.

Five teams have five points after taking the maximum amount from their opening game last week, while two sides are yet to put anything on the board.

All the team news for the five fixtures this weekend can be found below.

You can also listen to coverage of all of the matches on BBC DAB and FM local radio, via BBC Sounds or the BBC Sport website and app.

Bath make seven changes for the visit of Exeter as they prepare for their first home game since the Devon side won at The Rec in June's Prem semi-final.

Ciaran Donoghue is named at full-back in three changes to the backs, as centre Cameron Redpath and scrum-half Bernard van der Linde come in to partner Finn Russell in the half-backs.

Tom Dunn is named at hooker while Guy Pepper comes in for injured England flanker Sam Underhill as Ewan Richards and Quin Roux are also brought into the pack.

Exeter welcome back Tommy Wyatt after a minor shoulder problem as he gets his first Prem start since a serious knee injury in May 2025.

He comes in on the wing as Olly Woodburn moves to full-back with Ben Hammersley dropping out.

They are the only changes to an Exeter side that suffered a surprise 45-24 loss at home to Gloucester last week.

Bath: Donoghue; Cokanasiga, Lawrence, Redpath, De Glanville; Russell, Van der Linde; Obano, Dunn, Stuart; Roux, Ewels (c), Richards, Pepper, Du Preez.

Replacements: Frost, Kirk, Griffin, Hill, Reid, Carr-Smith, Ojomoh, Coetzee.
