Replacements: Gulley, Goodrick-Clarke, Tchumbadze, Beckerleg, Worley Brady, Wolstenholme, Haydon-Wood, Wimbush.

Bristol v Northampton (Saturday, 15:05 BST)

Bristol and Northampton have both made two changes apiece to their starting line-ups for this weekend's meeting.

Bears prop Jake Woolmore comes in for Ellis Genge, who misses out with a sprained wrist picked up against Sale that is likely to keep him out for two to three weeks, while flanker Steven Luatua starts having come on from the bench a week ago.

Saints came away with a record-breaking 94-33 win when the two sides met in May at Franklin's Gardens but the Prem champions have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

After scoring a hat-trick last week against Newcastle, Tommy Freeman moves to full-back with Ollie Sleightholme coming onto the wing. In the back row Josh Taylor gets his first Prem start with Callum Chick moving to the bench.

Bristol: Jordan; Rees-Zammit, Janse van Rensburg, Williams, Ibitoye; MacGinty, Randall; Woolmore, Oghre, Kloska; Rubiolo, Batley, Luatua, Grondona, Harding (c).

Replacements: Gwilliam, Chawatama, Halliwell, Taylor, Owen, Marmion, Pepper, Ivanishvili.

Northampton: Freeman; Sleightholme, Hutchinson, Dingwall (c), Hendy; F. Smith, McParland; Iyogun, Langdon, Kundiona; Coles, Prowse, Kemeny, Taylor, Pollock.

Replacements : R. Smith, Fischetti, Neculai, Lockett, Chick, Mitchell, Belleau, Pater.

Gloucester v Harlequins (Saturday, 17:30 BST)

Gloucester have been forced into changes to their back line following injuries sustained by Phil Cokanasiga and Ben Redshaw in the win against Exeter.

Cokanasiga had surgery on a foot injury earlier this week and may be out until January, while Redshaw failed a head injury assessment following the Exeter match.

George Barton and Ollie Thorley start at full-back and wing respectively, while Will Joseph shifts inside to centre.

Harlequins are again without fly-half Marcus Smith because of a finger injury, although head coach Jason Gilmore has said the England international should return within the next two weeks.

Prop Fin Baxter (foot) could also be back within the same timeframe, while full-back George Furbank is available again after a head injury and will make his first Prem appearance for Quins since joining from Northampton in the summer.

Newcastle v Leicester (Saturday, 19:45 BST)

Former New Zealand international Hoskins Sotutu makes his first start for Newcastle Red Bulls when they host Leicester Tigers on Saturday.

The number eight replaces Sam Graham, who drops to the bench, while the only other change to Newcastle's starting XV will be on the wing where Obi Ene comes in for his league debut for the club after Werner Kok was ruled out with a hamstring injury.

James Thompson and Orlando Bailey start for Leicester Tigers on their trip to Kingston Park, having both come off the bench in their opening weekend defeat by Saracens.

An injury suffered by Finn Carnduff in the narrow loss not only means Thompson takes his place in the pack, but it has also prompted Tom Manz to be called from his season-long loan deal with Cardiff Blues to take his place among Tigers' replacements.

articles.summary: Happy Friday, TSFers! This extra-long international break won’t wind up until Tuesday, but it’s time to start re-focusing on Arsenal. Unfortunately, we’ve go...
articles.body:
Happy Friday, TSFers! This extra-long international break won't wind up until Tuesday, but it's time to start re-focusing on Arsenal. Unfortunately, we've got an injury update coming later today for a couple guys who picked up issues on international duty. I don't like international breaks. I really don't like extended international breaks.

This morning, we'll talk about something fun. The NHL season started this week — go Caps — and with the season just a few days old, we've got something that only happens every couple of seasons . A goalie goal!

There weren't any goalie goals last season. Oddly enough, there were three the season before — Ilya Sorokin, Alex Nedeljkovic, and Filip Gustavsson. According to Wikipedia, that was the first time there had ever been more than one in an NHL season. To give a sense of how uncommon they are, there have only been 21 goalie goals in the history of the NHL. There have been multiple 5+ season stretches without one being scored. Martin Brodeur scored three in his career. Ron Hextall scored two.

With all that in mind, what other sporting feats are as rare and unlikely as the NHL goalie goal? The first thing that came to mind is a no-hitter in baseball. It's not quite there in terms of rarity — there have been 327 recorded in MLB history — but the combination of difficulty and rarity feels about right. What say y'all?

The hangover after a big win is real in College Football and the latest example could be the #8 Florida Gators (4-0) when they travel to #25 Missouri (3-1). Florida is coming off a 52-28 win over #4 Ole Miss a week after the Rebels beat LSU in a top 10 matchup, so the Gators know more than anyone they need to be locked in. Missouri is coming off a 31-24 loss to #24 Mississippi State where they held the lead entering the fourth quarter. The spread for this game is 5.5 points in favor of Florida and as you guessed it, most of the money is coming in on the top-10 ranked Gators.

Florida went belt to butt on Ole Miss. A 52-28 spanking ignited a Heisman campaign for Jadan Baugh and gave the world what they were looking for. After years falling short of expectations, the Gators look like they are going to live up to them. Baugh had 142 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 29 carries and Duke Clark added 126 yards and a score on 12 attempts. The Gators as a team ran for 302 yards and six touchdowns versus Ole Miss. Florida's defense held Ole Miss to 4-of-11 on third downs, two turnovers, and four TFL.

Missouri could have started 4-0, but blew a 24-17 lead entering the fourth quarter against Mississippi State. The Tigers were are without Ahmad Hardy while he's recovering from a gunshot wound, so Austin Simmons has been slinging for Mizzou. articles.title: Thursday night lights shine bright on Bengal volleyball
articles.summary: Oct. 2—For the first time ever, the lights at Lewiston High School's P1FCU Sports Complex shone over volleyball action. Laid out on the football field Thursd...
articles.body:
Oct. 2—For the first time ever, the lights at Lewiston High School's P1FCU Sports Complex shone over volleyball action.

Laid out on the football field Thursday was a temporary court supplied by Pacific Northwest Volleyball for a Class 5A Inland Empire League clash between the Lewiston Bengals and visiting Moscow Bears that doubled as the main attraction of Judy Fong Pink Night.

The Bengals were not about to disappoint the large-and-enthusiastic home crowd the unique spectacle drew, maintaining a steady edge over the Bears from the middle of the first set onward. With Lewiston up two sets and holding match point in the third, Madeline Taylor passed from the back row to junior opposite hitter Chloe Way, who delivered a spike that skipped off the top of the net on its way to becoming the match-clinching kill.

The final scoreline read 25-14, 25-19, 25-17.

"It was so energetic," Lewiston's Darby Litchfield said. "We had so much fun, and I'll definitely remember this experience for the rest of my life."

Each Lewiston starter was announced with a nickname in the pre-match ceremony, with monikers such as Kamdyn "K-Dog" Welker, Callie "C-Money" Fisher, Avery "The Bear" Balmer, Chloe "Legacy" Way, Tressa "Baby Giraffe" Lukehart and Emery "Mama" McKarcher. Some of them jogged toward the stands and launched pink balls into the crowd after their numbers were called.

Additional fanfare included pre- and mid-match light shows and a contest before the final frame in which spectators came down and attempted to win commemorative shirts laid across the court by serving balls onto them.

Bengal players interviewed afterward agreed that the match was memorable not only for the spectacle, but also for the conditions of playing under the stars on an unconventional surface.

"I feel like it gives a lot more bounce," Lukehart said of the court, which was considerably more pliable than a gymnasium hardwood. "You feel like you're kind of levitating above the turf."

Added junior middle blocker Elle Walker, "I've played beach volleyball, but this was way different with the tiled floor. It was cushiony."

Balmer (seven kills, 10 digs) and McKarcher (22 assists, five aces) topped the stat sheets on the day for Lewiston (10-6, 3-4).

Though they were neither the focus of the fanfare nor the victors of the match, the Bears (1-11-2, 0-4) took positives from the evening as well.

"It was an absolute blast," Moscow coach Kacey Cooper said. "I think all the coaches, all the players on both teams — I even think the student body for Lewiston and our own fans — had a blast doing something new and exciting. Both teams played well; yes, it was an adjustment to being outside, so it took a little bit, but overall, I think everyone played incredibly well with the change in venue."

Lauren Venzke (five kills), Leila Tiegs (seven digs) and Katherine Cummings (four assists) were the top statistical contributors for the Bears.

Both teams wore pink jerseys in keeping with a breast cancer awareness theme to the event honoring a former Bengal volleyball coach who passed away from the disease in 2014. The outdoor setup was modeled after a Nebraska Cornhuskers volleyball match held at their football stadium in 2023.

"I thought, 'Gosh that's a great concept,'" Lewiston coach Marie Huffman said. "Trying to implement it here at Lewiston, thankfully my athletic director (Doug Henderson) was like, 'Yeah, let's do it.'"

Among those in attendance — and participating in the event's pink theme — was longtime Lewis-Clark State tennis coach Kai Fong, the late Judy Fong's husband.

"It's always such a nice honor to have the community here supporting volleyball, and to have people remember her for a long time," he said. "Being an educator, it's always special for her; she would have loved to see this and be a part of all this. It's certainly very humbling to see all of this as a memorial and to see the kind of energy that's out here."

The LC State men's and women's tennis teams also attended wearing pink shirts in a surprise show of solidarity with their coach.

articles.title: Trail Blazers Fire Announcer Over Insensitive Teenage Tweets
articles.summary: The firing came the same day the Blazers announced Braiden Bell’s hiring
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers fired play-by-play announcer Braiden Bell the same day they announced his hire after a local reporter uncovered insensitive tweets from 2012 and 2013, when he was a teenager.

Devon Haskins, a reporter for Portland NBC affiliate KGW, found tweets from when Bell was about 15 years old. "I'm not racist at all.. But not gonna lie.. Asian people piss me off! Hahaha #Honest," Bell wrote in one of the tweets. In another, he wrote, "Gotta give a shoutout to all the big girls out there and those closet whores."

The Blazers fired the announcer after the reporter reached out to the organization for comment.

"The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist, or harmful comments," the team said in a statement posted on X/Twitter . "Social media posts made by our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster are in clear violation of team and league policies, as well as our values and expectations. Therefore, we will not be moving forward with this broadcaster."

Bell's agency didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The 29-year-old Bell was hired to the job on the Blazers' Rip City network after calling games for the Valley Suns in the G League, and the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury. KGW did not find any problematic tweets from when he was an adult.

Bell replaced Kevin Calabro, who had been Portland's play-by-play broadcaster for the past decade. Calabro recently joined a rotation of announcers for the Timberwolves that also includes Michael Grady and Jon "Boog" Sciambi.

"The play-by-play role carries a long legacy of excellence, on the broadcast and in character, and we hold that standard without exception," the Blazers' statement continued. "We did not meet our own bar in this process, and for that we apologize to Blazers fans and to Rip City. We strongly believe that everyone who is a part of Rip City should feel welcome and safe and we will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects these values. We will do better."

The Blazers' regular season kicks off on Oct. 21 with a home game against the Suns.

One of the Arizona Cardinals ' upcoming opponents has made a pretty big move with a trade for an excellent defensive player. The Dallas Cowboys acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers for a conditional sixth-round pick in 2027 and a second-round pick in 2028.

Porter, a 2023 second-round pick, broke up 14 passes last season.

He was locked with the Steelers in a contract stalemate. He also has missed the first three games of the season with a back issue, which he now says is fine. He made the call not to play in the first three games of the season.

The Cowboys, despite offseason changes to their defense, are ranked 25th in the league in points allowed. They are 1-2 and have allowed 28 or more points twice in three games.

Porter bolsters that defensive backfield.

The Cardinals will face the Cowboys on the road in Week 8, so Porter should be in shape and know Dallas' defense by then.

articles.title: Franchise royalty: Los Angeles Dodgers all‑time postseason lineup
articles.summary: Meet the Los Angeles Dodgers' all-time October lineup, from Roy Campanella and Sandy Koufax to Corey Seager and Kenley Jansen
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are heading into the 2026 MLB playoffs with 100 wins, the No. 2 seed in the National League, and a first-round bye as they try to pull off an incredible three-peat.

Los Angeles locked up win number 100 by beating the Giants 5-1 on Sept. 27. That also gave manager Dave Roberts his sixth 100-win season, tying the MLB record for the most by a manager, sharing it with Bobby Cox and Joe McCarthy. The club had another record-setting year off the field as well, drawing 4,034,219 fans.

Hardly any franchise west of the Bronx can match what the Dodgers have done in October. They've had legendary players in every era, starting back in Brooklyn and continuing all the way through their recent championship runs in L.A.

Putting together their best-ever playoff lineup isn't just about who put up big numbers in the regular season. What really counts is showing up in October, delivering in clutch moments, and carrying the team deep into the postseason.

We gathered all those clutch performers in one spot. Here's the Dodgers' all-time postseason lineup.

Today In 1951: Brooklyn #Dodgers catcher Roy Campanella wins his 1st N.L. MVP Award (he'd also win in '53 & '55) pic.twitter.com/KKfKXsJLcy — Baseball by BSmile (@BSmile) November 1, 2016

Today In 1951: Brooklyn #Dodgers catcher Roy Campanella wins his 1st N.L. MVP Award (he'd also win in '53 & '55) pic.twitter.com/KKfKXsJLcy

Baseball by BSmile (@BSmile) November 1, 2016

Roy Campanella gets the top spot in this lineup at catcher. He played 32 postseason games for the Brooklyn Dodgers and hit .237 during his October career.

Campanella hit four home runs and drove in 12 runs. He also posted a .696 OPS in those games.

His value went far beyond his offensive numbers. Campanella was the field general for the famous "Boys of Summer."

He worked with some of the greatest pitchers in Dodgers history. That included Don Newcombe and Sandy Koufax.

Campanella appeared in five World Series during the 1940s and 1950s. He also played a major role in the Dodgers' first championship in 1955.

His three MVP awards further highlight his importance to the franchise. Will Smith has built a strong modern postseason resume, but Campanella represents one of the most important eras in Dodgers history.

Los Angeles Dodgers Steve Garvey was honored during pregame ceremonies for the 40th anniversary of the 1981 World Series team at Dodger Stadium. Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)

Steve Garvey was one of the defining players of the Dodgers' championship teams. His postseason numbers remain among the best in franchise history.

Garvey played 45 postseason games with Los Angeles. He hit .346 with 10 home runs and 22 RBIs. His .942 OPS also shows how well he performed in October.

His consistency was especially impressive. Across four different postseasons with the Dodgers, Garvey never hit below .286.

He hit an incredible .385 during the 1974 postseason. Garvey also won NLCS MVP honors in 1978.

His postseason career included another championship run in 1981. Garvey anchored the Dodgers' infield during that World Series title.

Freddie Freeman has added his own major moments to Dodgers history, especially with his 2024 World Series MVP award and walkoff grand slam in Game 1 of that series. Garvey's long record of October production still earns him the first-base spot on this team.

Los Angeles Dodgers first base coach Davey Lopes against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Davey Lopes was one of the key pieces of the Dodgers' late-1970s and early-1980s teams. He played 45 postseason games.

Lopes hit .242 with six home runs and 22 RBIs during those games. He also stole 20 bases, including 10 in the title run of 1981.

His speed made him a constant threat at the top of the lineup. Lopes could also provide unexpected power when the Dodgers needed it.

He formed an important infield combination with Steve Garvey and Bill Russell. That group helped the Dodgers win the 1981 World Series.

Lopes also had a huge game in the 1978 World Series. He hit two home runs in Game 1.

His 20 postseason stolen bases remain represent the top total in Dodgers history. That combination of speed and power gives Lopes the second-base spot.

Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Corey Seager (5) walks out to the field before game one of the 2021 NLCS against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park. Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)

Corey Seager played 61 postseason games with the Dodgers. He hit .236 with 13 home runs and 36 RBIs.

Seager also posted a .777 OPS during his Dodgers postseason career. His biggest contribution came during the 2020 championship run.

That year, Seager became only the eighth player in MLB history to win both the League Championship Series MVP and World Series MVP in the same postseason. Jeremy Pena of the Houston Astros made it nine in 2022.

Seager hit five home runs in the NLCS, setting a single-series NLCS record. Another three came during the NLDS and World Series as the Dodgers ended their 32-year championship drought.

Seager shares second place with Justin Turner on the Dodgers' franchise record for postseason home runs. They are three behind Max Muncy. Seager's 2020 run remains one of the greatest individual postseason performances in franchise history.

Los Angeles Dodgers third baseman Justin Turner (10) throws to first bases for an out in the seventh inning against the San Diego Padres during game three of the NLDS for the 2022 MLB Playoffs at Petco Park. Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)

Justin Turner owns several major Dodgers postseason records. He played 86 postseason games for Los Angeles.

That is the most in franchise history. Turner also holds the Dodgers' postseason records for hits and RBIs, with 85 hits and 42 RBIs.

His overall postseason line includes a .270 batting average, 13 home runs and a .830 OPS. Those numbers came across several deep playoff runs.

Turner became known for delivering important hits when the Dodgers needed them most. His biggest moment came in Game 2 of the 2017 NLCS.

He hit a walk-off home run on the 29th anniversary of Kirk Gibson's famous home run in Game 1 of the 1988 World Series. The moment added another memorable chapter to Dodgers postseason history.

His combination of longevity, production and big October moments makes Turner the third baseman.

Los Angeles Dodgers left fielder Joc Pederson (31) is congratulated as he enters the dugout after hitting a home run against the Tampa Bay Rays during the first inning during game five of the 2020 World Series at Globe Life Field. Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)

Joc Pederson earned the nickname "Joctober" because of his postseason performances. He played 64 playoff games with the Dodgers.

Pederson hit .272 during those games. He also hit nine home runs, drove in 20 runs and posted a .852 OPS.

His 2017 World Series was particularly impressive. Pederson hit .333 with three home runs and five RBIs across the seven-game series.

He also posted a 1.344 OPS during that World Series. His left-handed power gave the Dodgers another dangerous bat during several October runs.

Pederson continued to provide important home runs during the 2020 championship run. His postseason production earned him a place among the franchise's most memorable October hitters.

Duke Snider was one of the biggest stars of the Dodgers' Brooklyn era. He played 36 postseason games, and every one came in the World Series.

Snider hit .286 with 11 home runs and 26 RBIs. His .945 OPS shows how well he performed when the stakes were highest.

He also holds a remarkable World Series record. Snider is the only player in MLB history to hit four home runs in two different World Series.

He hit four in 1952 and repeated the feat in 1955, leading the Dodgers to their first crown. His 11 World Series home runs remain a National League record.

That production makes Snider an easy choice for one of the three outfield spots.

Los Angeles Dodgers center fielder Cody Bellinger (35) advances to third base during the seventh inning of game two of the NLDS for the 2022 MLB Playoffs against the San Diego Padres at Dodger Stadium. Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)

Cody Bellinger played 69 postseason games with Los Angeles. He hit .211 with nine home runs and 33 RBIs during those games.

Bellinger also stole 14 bases. His overall postseason batting average does not fully explain his importance to the Dodgers.

He won the 2018 NLCS MVP award after helping Los Angeles reach the World Series. Two years later, Bellinger hit the game-winning home run in Game 7 of the 2020 NLCS.

That home run sent the Dodgers to the World Series. His defense also played a major role during that postseason.

Bellinger's home-run-robbing catch against Fernando Tatis Jr. in the 2020 NLDS became one of the most memorable defensive plays of the Dodgers' recent playoff history.

His power, speed and center-field defense make him one of the three outfielders on this team.

Los Angeles Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy (13) celebrates after hitting a solo home run during the eighth inning against the San Francisco Giants at Dodger Stadium. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Max Muncy gives this lineup another powerful left-handed bat. He has played 79 postseason games for the Dodgers and hit 16 home runs.

That total puts Muncy alone at the top of the Dodgers' all-time postseason home run leaderboard. He also has driven in 37 runs and posted a .817 OPS.

Muncy's plate discipline made him especially dangerous in October. His ability to work counts and draw walks often created opportunities for the hitters around him.

One of his most memorable moments came in the 2018 World Series. Muncy hit a walk-off home run in the 18th inning of Game 3 against the Boston Red Sox.

That game remains the longest in World Series history. The home run also became one of the defining moments of Muncy's Dodgers career.

Sandy Koufax speaks on during an unveiling ceremony for the brand new Koufax commemorative statue at the Centerfield Plaza at Dodger Stadium. Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)

Sandy Koufax has one of the greatest postseason pitching records in Dodgers history. He made eight postseason appearances and started seven of them.

Koufax went 4-3 with a 0.95 ERA across 57 innings. He struck out 61 batters and posted a 0.825 WHIP. His October record also includes four complete games and two shutouts.

His World Series performances made his postseason legacy even stronger. Koufax won World Series MVP honors in both 1963 and 1965.

The defining moment came in Game 7 of the 1965 World Series. Koufax took the mound on only two days' rest and pitched a shutout.

That performance helped the Dodgers win the championship. His sub-1.00 ERA over 57 World Series innings remains one of the most remarkable postseason pitching records in baseball history.

Los Angeles Dodgers relief pitcher Kenley Jansen (74) reacts to the last out in the ninth inning against the Atlanta Braves during Game 6 of the 2020 NLCS . Mandatory Credit: Tim Heitman-USA TODAY Sports (Reuters)

Kenley Jansen owns several Dodgers postseason records. He appeared in 57 playoff games for Los Angeles. That is the most in franchise history.

Jansen also pitched 63 1/3 postseason innings as a reliever. That is another Dodgers record. His 19 saves are also the most in franchise history.

Across those 57 games, Jansen posted a 2.13 ERA. He struck out 92 batters and finished with a 0.805 WHIP. Those numbers show how reliable he was during the Dodgers' long playoff runs.

The 2017 postseason was one of his best stretches. Jansen threw 16 2/3 innings and allowed only three earned runs. He also struck out 20 batters.

His cutter became one of the biggest weapons in the Dodgers' bullpen. For several seasons, opposing teams had to get through Jansen to finish off Los Angeles.

articles.title: How Round Rock can still make a UIL playoff run after rough loss to Westlake football
articles.summary: Round Rock lost to Westlake 38-17 in a District 25-6A Central Texas high school football game Thursday at Chaparral Stadium.
articles.body:
It's on to the next game for Round Rock.

And though it will take the Dragons longer to get back on the field than they'd probably like after Thursday's 38-17 loss to Westlake at Chaparral Field, Round Rock has plenty left on the table.

But as Dragons coach Cody Moore noted, Round Rock will have to play better the rest of its District 25-6A slate, especially against Lake Travis and Cedar Ridge, if it wants to accomplish some of its goals.

"It's a long season, and this was only the second district game," said Moore, whose team went 3-1 against a grueling nondistrict schedule. "But it definitely makes us go back to the drawing board. Makes us realize that there's a lot of work to do and we're not there yet."

Round Rock (4-2, 1-1) is still in the district title race, heading into the off week. But it's going to need help. And it's also going to need to beat Lake Travis. The Dragons also have three fellow Round Rock ISD schools left to play - they beat Stony Point in their district opener - to try and get into the 6A Division I playoffs and win a postseason game for the first time since 2020.

Moore said he'll use the time off as a bit of a reset. Despite the disappointing loss on a soggy Thursday night, Round Rock owns impressive wins over Dripping Springs and Vandegrift

"We'll go back to the fundamentals," he said. "Go back to what makes us us, and just get better at the things that we hold true and what we're all about."

Round Rock is mostly about a good passing attack. It's possible the rainy weather conditions Thursday hampered a previously high-flying Dragons offense that saw quarterback Dov Stickler enter the game with 1,376 yards and 17 TDs through the air. But that's an unknown theoretical, and Moore said his team made too many errors.

"Our offense did a good job moving the ball up and down the field, but when you have three turnovers, it's hard to overcome that," he said. "Westlake did a good job defensively. … When you play good teams and play guys that don't make mistakes, you can't make mistakes."

Westlake coach Tony Salazar said his team respected Round Rock coming into its district opener, which led to a good week of practice.

"No. 17 (Dylan Jaeger) is pretty talented, and every time you see him on tape, he's breaking through tackles and going for 60 or 70," Salazar said of the talented tight end and wide receiver. "They're a physical, good football team. … That led to our kids knowing that we better show up and work because we got a football team coming to play us. And that's exactly what happened."

articles.body: Francia recibe a Bélgica este lunes en el Stade de France, apenas una semana después de ganarle 0-1 en Bruselas. La selección de Zinedine Zidane ha ganado sus dos primeros partidos de la era post-Deschamps, ambos por la mínima y sin encajar: 0-1 en Turquía, con gol de Mbappé, y 0-1 en Bruselas, con un golazo de Olise en el minuto 88. Bélgica, que debutó con un 0-2 en Roma ante Italia, llega con la necesidad de cambiar una dinámica muy adversa. Los Diablos Rojos no ganan a Francia en un partido oficial desde 1981 y encadenan seis derrotas seguidas ante su vecino. Favorito para el partido entre Francia y Bélgica Las casas de apuestas se inclinan por el local. En 1XBet, la victoria de Francia aparece de forma provisional a cuota 1.54, mientras que el empate a 4.46 y el triunfo belga a 5.45. El equipo de Zidane llega sin Mbappé, lesionado de la rodilla, pero conserva un frente de ataque con Dembélé, Olise, Doué y Barcola. En el último duelo, Francia dominó con un 65 % de posesión, 18 disparos frente a 12 y siete tiros a puerta frente a dos, y se topó con las paradas de Lammens, además de un larguero de Doué y un poste de Da Cunha. Número de goles de Francia Este mercado resulta de lo más interesante. Pese a su dominio, Francia solo ha marcado un gol en cada uno de sus dos partidos, y los dos llegaron con el reloj muy avanzado en el caso de Olise. La falta de Mbappé reduce la contundencia de un equipo que genera mucho pero remata con poca precisión. Bélgica, por su parte, ha mostrado orden defensivo y solo ha concedido un gol en dos partidos. Con esos datos en las apuestas deportivas de 1XBET, que Francia marque dos goles se paga a 1.44, por 2.65 del caso contrario. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta a un partido cerrado. Ninguno de los cuatro encuentros que han disputado ambas selecciones en esta Nations League ha superado los 2.5 goles: Turquía 0-1 Francia, Italia 0-2 Bélgica y Bélgica 0-1 Francia. Aunque Bélgica tiene calidad arriba con De Bruyne, Godts y Lukebakio, la solidez defensiva de Maignan y compañía y la cautela de dos selecciones nuevas inclinan la balanza. Pese a ello, 1XBET paga a 1.46 que el encuentro tenga 3 o más goles, por 2.49 del caso contrario. Marcador al descanso y al final El último precedente ofrece una pista clara: 0-0 al descanso y gol decisivo en el tramo final. Zidane, que ya cambió nueve jugadores entre un partido y otro, tiene mucha profundidad de plantel para refrescar el ataque en la segunda parte, mientras que Bélgica tiende a sostenerse en bloque bajo durante más de una hora. Nuestro pronóstico es un 0-0 al descanso y un 1-0 final, o lo que es lo mismo, empate al descanso y victoria de Francia al final, a cuota 4.5 en 1XBET. Pero también os dejamos el resto de opciones.

articles.title: Arch Manning is leading an average Texas offense. Here are 2 Longhorns who could help
articles.summary: Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian aimed to fix an average Longhorns offense during the bye week. Here are three concerns for that side of the ball.
articles.body:
For a few minutes in his team's 20-17 win last Saturday at Tennessee, the Texas football offense looked like what head coach Steve Sarkisian envisioned when he helped construct one of the highest-paid units in the nation.

The Longhorns opened the game in Knoxville with an eight-play, 75-yard scoring drive capped by a 9-yard touchdown run from Raleek Brown. And they pulled off the possession with textbook precision; quarterback Arch Manning completed all three of his passes for 56 yards, Brown and Derek Cooper combined on five runs for a total of 16 yards, and the Longhorns didn't commit one penalty.

Perfect balance, perfect execution, perfect result.

"I was really impressed with the offense, the way we started the game," Sarkisian said. "To get the ball in that environment and take the lead 7-0 on the road, I thought was really big for us about owning the environment, owning the arena."

But what happened the rest of the game bothered Sarkisian, who has also served as the team's play-caller since he took over the Texas program for the 2021 season.

Over its next nine possessions, Texas produced six three-and-outs, a turnover and a pair of field goals as well as five penalties. The Longhorns did help seal the win with an eight-play, 60-yard touchdown drive late in the fourth quarter, but Sarkisian knows his team can't afford such offensive dry spells in an upcoming eight-game SEC schedule that includes five meetings with teams in the current Associated Press poll as well as rivalry games against Oklahoma and Texas A&M.

"From that point forward (on the opening drive), until about the second-to-last offensive drive, we did not play very good offensive football," he said. "I'd love to say it was this or that. It literally was us taking turns of not doing the things that we had practiced to do, and that was unfortunate because sometimes it's easier to say this one position group or this one player or this one thing was the issue, and it really wasn't."

So, how can No. 1 Texas (4-0, 1-0 SEC) improve on an offense that ranks 11th in the SEC in scoring with 33.3 points a game and 12th in total offense with 378.5 yards per contest? That's something Sarkisian plans on figuring out before the Longhorns resume their SEC schedule Oct. 10 in the Red River Rivalry with Oklahoma.

"That'll be the task this week (and) throughout the bye week of where we need to improve offensively and where we can build upon that," he said. "But again, I'd love to say, 'Man, it was just the right tackle or the right guard or the center or the left guard or the tight ends.' But it was like each play somebody else was kind of taking their turn. So we've got to get that rectified. We've got to get these guys believing in in their training and trusting their training to perform."

Here are three specific questions for the Texas offense entering the heart of its schedule:

Will Hollywood Smothers' return create explosive runs?

Brown ran hard against Tennessee with 67 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries, but the Longhorns didn't heavily invest in the backfield during the offseason just for effort. They want explosiveness, and the likely return of Hollywood Smothers against Oklahoma could help.

Smothers suffered an ankle injury Sept. 19 in the 30-6 win over UITSA and did not play at Tennessee after going through pregame warmups.

"He was an emergency (option) for us Saturday," Sarkisian said Monday. "I think he'll be fine in a couple weeks when we play OU."

Tre Wisner and CJ Baxter, who shared the bulk of the backfield duties across the previous two seasons, both left in the portal. The Longhorns shelled out an undisclosed amount of money for Brown and Smothers, each of whom earned all-conference honors a year ago at Arizona State and North Carolina State, respectively. So far this season, Smothers leads the team with 198 yards rushing on 41 carries while Brown has 196 yards on 48 carries. But the team has just three carries that have gone for more than 15 yards; Smothers has a 45-yarder and an 18-yarder, and Brown has a 21-yard carry.

Can WR Cam Coleman emerge as a consistent playmaker?

Receiver Cam Coleman signed with Texas as arguably the most coveted and, presumably, the most compensated nonquarterback in the portal. But through four games, the Auburn transfer has just 12 catches albeit with a team-high four touchdowns and a 17.3 yards-per-catch average.

Can Manning get Coleman involved more in the passing game, and does that even matter for a deep unit that also includes Ryan Wingo (19 catches, 239 yards), Emmett Mosley V (12 catches, 173 yards) and emerging freshman Jermaine Bishop Jr. (six catches, 81 yards)? And does Manning need to force the ball to Coleman, which he seemed to do on a deep pass to the post against Tennessee that led to an interception?

According to Sarkisian, the questions don't matter. Coleman opens things up for the entire offense, Sarkisian said, which helped Manning complete 14 of 19 passes for 201 yards against the Vols.

"There was a lot of emphasis and attention drawn his way with cloud coverage and things, and that's where we have to utilize the other guys," Sarkisian said.

And about that long pass to Coleman that led to the pick?

"I have no qualms about (Manning) taking that shot, and I like Cam Coleman's odds one on one on a deep ball down the field," Sarkisian said. "But we've got to be creative enough, and we've got to allow him to do the things that he does really well as we continue to navigate our way through the season."

What happened to Arch Manning's pass protection?

Texas signed three offensive linemen in the portal - guards Dylan Sikorski and Laurence Seymore III and tackle Melvin Siani - to bolster a unit whose primary goal is to protect Manning. So, what happened to the pass protection against Tennessee? Manning went down four times in the first three games of the season but endured six sacks and two more hits against Tennessee.

"It's a combination of things," Sarkisian said. "It clearly was not good enough Saturday."

Coaches tend to dismiss the ratings system utilized by Pro Football Focus. But for what it's worth, PFF gives left guard Sikorksi a season-long pass-blocking grade of 92.1, the best among all the starting linemen. Right guard Brandon Baker ranks the lowest for the season with a 74.4. Every other starter ranks between 79.4 and 85.4.

Against Tennessee, Sikorski led the team with an 86.7 pass-blocking grade followed by Siani (73.4), center Connor Robertson (67.1), left tackle Trevor Goosby (63.7) and Baker (44.4).

articles.title: Luke Wafle needs to lead USC football's pass rush to a dominant day
articles.summary: Luke Wafle will have a game-wrecking performance against Washington in Week 5. He needs to, because the Huskies' O-line isn't very good
articles.body:
The USC Trojans ' pass rush has been nonexistent for all but one game this season. The Trojans have yet to create a game in which one of their defensive linemen has a monster sack-production performance. Their upcoming opponent, the Washington Huskies , could open the door for that to finally happen.

Luke Wafle has impressed and flashed many times to start the season. My hot take of the week is that Wafle will not only get his first sack of the season against Washington, but he will also have multiple sacks in Week 5. The time for a huge breakout game for Wafle is overdue.

The Huskies are coming off a game where they gave up 7 total sacks against the Minnesota Gophers . This is a unit that the Trojans' defensive line needs to take full advantage of. I think Wafle will lead in that aspect and have his most dominant performance yet. Waffle has gotten in the backfield and had tackles for loss and pressures. In this game, he will finish on pass downs.

Getting sacks is the only thing Wafle is missing in his game to become more of a game-wrecker off the edge. Wafle does just about everything else, even linebackers in coverage, and holds his own. This game will be the beginning for a player who will become one of the most elite defensive players in the Big Ten and the country. Wafle's 2 sacks will help the Trojans' defense put together their best showing since Week 1 and help the Trojans get a much-needed win.

Contact/Follow @TrojansWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of USC Trojans news, notes and opinion .

articles.title: Stats and Snaps – 2026 Week 3, Commanders vs Seahawks
articles.summary: Backs against the wall, the Commanders pull off the upset of the season, so far
articles.body:
The Commanders took the field in their home opener against the Seahawks, reeling from the Week 2 loss of their starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, adding to the injury attrition of key starters including LT Laremy Tunsil, RG Sam Cosmi, S Nick Cross, LB Frankie Luvu and TE Chig Okonkwo.

The injury concerns were further compounded by the underperformance of secondary players Mike Sainristil, Quan Martin and Jeremy Reaves, combined with growing doubts about leadership of the head coach and new schemes on both sides of the ball being spearheaded by novice coordinators. Around the league, confidence in the Commanders was tanking following the devastating 20-37 Week 2 loss to the Cowboys. The Vegas line had the Commanders as 8.5 point underdogs at home, against the visiting Seahawks.

What took place was a reminder of the generally mis-quoted, but nonetheless apt movie line about what can happen "on any given Sunday". The rag-tag band of injury replacements, disrespected, and underrated players rallied around journeyman backup Marcus Mariota, who led an efficient offense that did enough to capitalize on opportunities generated by the defense, while avoiding turnovers.

The defense was strong against the run (9 th fewest rushing yards allowed Week 3), but continued to struggle against the pass (32 nd in passing yards allowed).

The key to victory was generating 3 turnovers which led to points, compared to the Seahawks' 0. Historically, teams with a +3 turnover differential have a 90.7% win rate. That is a tremendous obstacle for a opponent to overcome. As good as Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks' passing attack may be, on Sunday it was not enough.

In Week 3, missing their star QB and key starters on both sides of the ball, against the reigning Super Bowl champs, the Commanders' offense ranked 20 th in the league in weighted EPA/Play at +0.04, while the defense ranked 11 th at -0.045:

The upset win was the result of total team effort. Players making that kind of effort, in the face of the type of adversity the Commanders were facing, points to coaching and leadership perhaps being better than was widely appreciated.

While the overall game left plenty of room for improvement, there were some standout performances on both sides of the ball, as well as continued struggles from players who have underperformed, and another key loss to injury.

As the Commanders seek to carry the momentum with them to London, let's take a look at who stepped up, who struggled and where everyone played in the biggest upset of the 2026 season so far.

These plays had the biggest impact on a team's scoring potential on a drive, as quantified by Expected Points Added (EPA). Cutoff: EPA = +/- 2.2

Q3, 10:50, 2 nd and 8 at SEA 30: Marcus Mariota pass complete deep left to Terry McLaurin for 30 yards, touchdown. EPA 3.83

Q2, 6:51, 2 nd and 9 at SEA 11: Marcus Mariota pass complete short middle to Treylon Burks for 11 yards, touchdown. EPA 2.73

Q4, 8:40, 4 th and 1 at SEA 40: Marcus Mariota pass complete short left to Terry McLaurin for 6 yards. EPA 2.72

Q4, 10:35, 3 rd and 13 at WAS 37: Marcus Mariota pass incomplete deep left intended for Terry McLaurin. Penalty on AJ Finley: Personal Foul / Defense, 15 yards (accepted). EPA 2.42

Q4, 1:55, 3 rd and 9 at WAS 34: Rachaad White right end for 19 yards. EPA 2.42

Q2, 0:03, 4 th and 2 at SEA 39: Drew Stevens 57 yard field goal. EPA 2.34

Q2, 1:51, 4 th and 2 at WAS 2: Sam Darnold pass incomplete short right intended for AJ Barner -defended by Jeremy Reaves. EPA -2.87

Q3, 12:09, 1 st and 10 at SEA 32: Sam Darnold pass short left, defended by Tim Settle, is intercepted by Sonny Styles at SEA-42 and returned for -1 yards. EPA -3.79

Q1, 11:06, 1 st and 10 at SEA 20: Jadarian Price left end for 1 yard, tackled by Sonny Styles, fumble forced by Amik Robertson, recovered by Tim Settle at SEA-21 (original fumble ruling overturned by replay assistant). EPA -4.45

Q4, 4:09, 2 nd and 15 at WAS 49: Sam Darnold pass short middle intended for AJ Barner is intercepted by Kain Medrano at 50 and returned for 50 yards, touchdown. EPA -8.44

Q1, 0:05, 1 st and 10 at WAS 21: Sam Darnold pass complete short left to Brady Russell for 20 yards (tackle by Quan Martin). EPA 2.8

Q2, 4:57, 3 rd and 14 at SEA 42: Sam Darnold pass complete deep left to Cooper Kupp for 16 yards (tackle by Mike Sainristil). EPA 2.56

Q2, 0:57, 4 th and 8 at WAS 39: Jason Myers 57 yd field goal. EPA 2.34

Q3, 6:14, 1 st and 10 at WAS 13: Sam Darnold pass complete short left to Eric Saubert for 13 yards. Fumble forced by Sonny Styles is recovered by Eric Saubert in end zone, touchdown. EPA 2.29

Q1, 0:54, 2 nd and 4 at SEA 47: Sam Darnold pass complete short right to AJ Barner for 32 yards (tackle by K'Lavon Chaisson). EPA 2.24

Q4, 11:57, 2 nd and 5 at WAS 11: Sam Darnold pass complete short left to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for 11 yards, touchdown. EPA 2.24

Marcus Mariota entered the game with a 2-0 career record as a starter against the Seahawks. He preserved the perfect record with a methodical and largely mistake free performance.

Marcus completed 19/31 passes (61.3%, 8.3 yd ADOT) for 183 yards and 3 TD, with 0 INT. He took 2 sacks for 7 yds and a whopping 9 QB hits. According to PFF, he was pressured on 48.6% of dropbacks.

Mariota had 5 rushing attempts for 11 yds (2.2 Y/A), including a 9 yard scamper for a first down on 3 rd and 7 with 1:36 remaining to secure the victory.

Mariota's 61.2 Total QBR ranked 15 th among starting QBs in Week 3.

Bill Croskey-Merritt led the team in rushing attempts (19), yards (36), first downs (3) and, believe it or not, rushing success rate (26.3%). But he only averaged 1.9 Y/A.

It was tough going for the Commanders runners, against the stout Seahawks' front 7. Bill, in particular, averaged just 1.0 yard before contact per rushing attempt (YBC/att).

Bill caught his only passing target for 7 yds. He also allowed 0 pressures in 8 pass blocking snaps and earned a team-high 78.3 pass blocking grade from PFF.

Rachaad White had the higher rushing average (4.4 Y/A), but that was largely due to a single 19 yd run, which accounted for 54% of his 35 yd rushing total in 8 attempts. Consequently, his rushing success rate (12.5%) was less than half of Bill's already meagre figure. Rachaad averaged a healthy 3.1 YBC/att. Rachaad caught his lone target for 6 yds.

Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in receiving yards for the first time this season. He caught 6/9 targets (66.7%) for 77 yards and 1 TD, at an 11.2 yd ADOT. He was the second most productive receiver on the team at an impressive 2.48 Y/RR. He was also a perfect 3/3 on contested targets and gave Marcus Mariota a 130.3 Passer Rating when targeted.

Stefon Diggs was second on the team with 33 yds on 4 out 7 targets (57.1%, 4.7 yd ADOT). Stefon had by far his least productive game for the Commanders, at a modest 1.22 Y/RR.

Jaylin Lane was third on the team with 21 receiving yards on a single reception 2 yards behind the line of scrimmage, with 23 yards gained after the catch. That play was one of only 2 routes he ran, resulting in a team-leading 10.5 Y/RR.

Antonio Williams had a somewhat disappointing day after the hot start to his rookie season. He caught 2/4 targets for just 15 yds.

Treylon Burks was a solid 2/2 for 13 yds and 1 TD.

Dyami Brown went 0/1, because he was unable to keep both feet in bounds on a 22 yd reception.

John Bates led the TEs in receiving by virtue of catching his lone target for 9 yds. Bates was penalized 5 yds for a false start in the 2 nd quarter.

Colson Yankoff caught 1/2 targets for 2 yds. Yankoff had the highest run blocking grade on the team at 67.8, per PFF.

Ben Sinnott failed to come down with his only target. But he did lead the team in snaps taken at fullback.

LT Brandon Coleman allowed 4 pressures in 35 opportunities in pass protection, including 1 QB hit. His 11.4% pressure rate is about twice what it should be for his position. That figure is right around his 11.8% average through three games this season. His 49.7 run blocking grade left a lot of room for improvement in London.

LG Chris Paul continued his excellent run in pass protection, allowing just 1 pressure and team low 2.9% pressure rate among the starting OL. His 42.5 run blocking grade was substandard, and his worst of the season thus far.

Lucas Patrick started his first game at center for the Commanders, allowing Nick Allegretti to slide to RG in place of Sam Cosmi, who is suffering a concussion. Patrick allowed 1 QB hit and 1 hurry in pass protection. His 6.3% pressure rate is below the starting level for centers, based on 2025 stats. On the other hand, his 60.1 run blocking grade was the second highest among the OL starters.

RG Nick Allegretti had a shocking game in pass protection, allowing 1 sack, 2 QB hits and 3 hurries, for an alarming 17.1% pressure rate. Alarmingly, his 52.8 run blocking grade was better than 2 of his fellow OL starters.

RT Josh Conerly Jr allowed just 2 QB hurries for a starting-level 5.7% pressure rate. His 62.2 run blocking grade was the highest of the OL starters, and second highest on the team after Yankoff. The one blemish on his game was a 5 yd false start penalty in the first quarter.

Odafe Oweh made 5 tackle assists and contributed to 1 run stop. In the pass rush he recorded 2 QB hits and 3 hurries, resulting in a 17.2% pressure rate, the highest among the front 7.

K'Lavon Chaisson made 3 tackles with 1 TFL. In the pass rush, he recorded 1 QB hit (4.3% pressure rate). K'Lavon dropped into coverage 11 times, representing 32.4% of passing downs. There was some disagreement among stats services, with PFF crediting him with 3 rec for 31 yds and PFR calling it 2 rec for 26 yds.

K'Lavon was called for a 15 yard unnecessary roughness penalty in the fourth quarter.

Joshua Josephs only played 15 defensive snaps but was involved in plays on 7 of them (47%). He recorded 2 tackles and 2 assists with 1 TFL and 2 defensive stops. He dropped into coverage 6 times (60% of pass plays), and allowed 3 rec/3 tgt for 37 yds.

Dorance Armstrong made 1 tackle, and recorded 3 QB hurries in the pass rush (12.0% pressure rate).

Javon Kinlaw had 2 tackle assists, contributing to 1 run stop. In the pass rush, he recorded 1 QB hit and 2 hurries. His 10.7% pressure rate led the iDL.

Tim Settle played a big part in two of the biggest plays of the game. He recovered the Jadarian Price forced by Amik Robertson in the first quarter. He also headed a Sam Darnold pass at the line for a PBU, deflecting the ball to set up Kain Medrano's pick-six. He also recorded 1 tackle.

Daron Payne had 1 tackle assist, contributing to a run stop. He generated 2 QB hurries in the pass rush (5.7% pressure rate).

Charles Omenihu had 1 tackle assist and generated 2 QB hurries (5.7% pressure rate).

Rookie Sonny Styles was named NFC Player of the Week for a standout performance featuring 4 tackles, 1 assist, 1 QB hit, 1 INT, 2 PBU, and 1 FF. There was some disagreement on his coverage stats, with PFF recording a decent 2 rec for 47 yds (1.07 Y/Cov Snp), while PFR recorded a less impressive 4 rec for 62 yds (1.41 Y/Cov Snp). Both services credited him with 1 missed tackle.

Leo Chenal suffered a neck fracture requiring season-ending surgery. Dan Quinn reported that the surgery went well, and he has feeling in all his extremities. It could have been much worse. Before the injury, Chenal recorded 2 tackles and 1 assist, with 1 TFL and 2 run stops. He also recorded 1 QB hurry in 3 blitz attempts.

Kain Medrano replaced Chenal, and was awarded a game ball for making the highest impact play of the game, a 50 yd pick-six in the fourth quarter. As Mark Tyler observed in the Studs and Duds , Kain had an up and down performance. In addition to the INT, he recorded 3 tackles and 2 assists, with 1 stop and 2 missed tackles.

There was some disagreement about Kain's coverage stats, with numbers ranging from bad to terrible. PFR recorded 5 rec/7 tgt for 46 yds (1.59 Y/Cov Snp); while PFF recorded 7 rec/7 tgt for 71 yds (2.45 Y/Cov). The NFL credits him with 1 PBU to go with the INT.

Amik Robertson tied with Jeremy Reaves as the team's leading tackler, with 4 tackles and 2 assists. He was the undisputed leader in impact tackles, with 4 defensive stops, 1 against the run and 3 on pass plays. He also made 1 FF and missed 1 tackle.

Robertson played most of the game at right CB. There was consensus that he allowed 53 yds and 1 TD in 49 coverage snaps with 4 PBUs, but disagreement about the number of targets and receptions. His rate of yardage allowed in the game (1.08 Y/Cov Snap) is right around average for starting CBs, based on 2025 season stats.

Rasul Douglas took over the bulk of the load at left CB, with Mike Sainristil moving inside. He made 3 tackles, with 1 stop on a pass play.

Despite some disagreement about the number of targets and receptions allowed, there was consensus that he allowed 57 yds (1.73 Y/Cov Snp) and recorded 1 PBU. His rate of yardage allowed through three games is below expectations for a starting CB, and well above his 2025 figure.

Mike Sainristil played nickel and had a reduced snap count compared to Weeks 1 and 2. He recorded 2 tackles, with 1 stop on a pass play. He was also penalized 5 yds for defensive holding in the third quarter.

There was slight disagreement on his coverage stats, but either way the verdict was not good. PFF recorded 3/3 for 36 yds (1.5 Y/Cov Snp); while PFR saw 4/4 for 41 yds (1.71 Y/Cov Snp). There was consensus that he allowed 2 TDs.

Fabian Moreau rotated in at LCB with Douglas. In 16 coverage snaps, he allowed 1 rec/1 tgt for a 1 yd TD (0.06 Y/Cov Snap). The TD was obviously not what you'd hope to see, but the rate of yardage allowed was encouraging, albeit in a small sample.

Jeremy Reaves took the most snaps at free safety. He tied Amik with 4 tackles and 2 assists, but only made 1 run stop. There was disagreement regarding his coverage stats (PFF: 24 yds, 0.53 Y/Cov Snp; PFR: 44 yds, 0.98 Y/Cov Snp). The NFL recorded 1 PBU.

Quan Martin also played FS and recorded 4 tackles and 1 assist. There was strong disagreement regarding his coverage stats (PFF: 1 rec, 17 yds, 0.40 Y/Cov Snp; PFR: 2 rec, 48 yds, 1.14 Y/Cov Snp). Quan drew a 2 yd pass interference penalty in the second quarter.

Percy Butler made 2 tackles and 1 assist. PFR recorded a 12 yd reception allowed in coverage, but not PFF.

Drew Stevens went 3/4 on extra points and was a perfect 2/2 on field goals, hitting from 36 and 57 yds. Stevens was penalized for kicking the ball out of bounds in the third quarter, giving the Seahawks the ball on the 40 yard line.

Tress Way booted 7 punts for 343 total yards, with 3 returns for 29 yds, resulting in a net average of 42 yds per punt.

In his first appearance of 2026, Luke McCaffrey returned 3 kicks for 90 yds (30 Y/A).

Rachaad White returned 1 kick for 38 yds.

Jaylin Lane made 2 fair catches on punts. The Seahawks' Michael Dickson did a great job of kicking the ball away from him.

Percy Butler edged out the other core special teamers with 1 tackle and 1 assist.

Ale Kaho , Tyler Owens , Jeremy Reaves , Ben Sinnott and Joshua Josephs each recorded 1 tackle in coverage.

There were no missed tackles on special teams, nor penalties, aside from Stevens' kick out of bounds.

articles.title: Camden Chat Pre-Season Contest Results
articles.summary: 282 entries, 30 questions, five winners.
articles.body:
If you have been a Camden Chat regular over the years, you are probably familiar with our annual contest. Each year in March, we post a series of questions to get you thinking about the season ahead. This past March , we had 282 of Camden Chat's finest submit their answers to 30 questions, and we had a pretty large group of first place finishers.

With 19 answers correct, congratulations go out to Melvinmora , J(O's)elskil , OldOsFan , DJDrP , and PaulFolk ! You five have proven your brilliance and may commence gloating immediately. One of these winners is my husband! I'll let you guess who.

Eight entrants had 18 correct answers, including our boss Mark Brown, AKA Eat More Esskay . Fun fact, the worse the Orioles do in a season, the higher Mark scores in this contest.* As for me, I finished in 63rd place with 15 correct.

*I did not check my work on this over multiple seasons, but you have to admit it sounds right.

To see the full results and find your score, click over to the results spreadsheet . It is sorted by number correct, so the easiest way is to CTRL+F your name. Check it out and let us know how you did in the comments!

The full questions and answers are below. This year was tough, as so many answers brought back all the troubles the team had. But on the bright side, next year our expectations will be so low that it'll be easier to be pleased with the results.

Innings pitched by Shane Baz or Grayson Rodriguez? Baz – 179.2; Grayson – 98.2 – Baz was a vast improvement over Rodriguez. No only did he pitch 81 more innings, but his ERA was 1.91 runs lower. (97.5% answered correctly)

Games played by guys named Tyler or guys named Jackson? Jackson – 200 (Hollday – 98, Jeremiah – 102), Tyler – 128 (O'Neill – 85, Wells – 43). This race was actually tied about halfway through the season before Team Jackson pulled away. (72% answered correctly)

Saves by Ryan Helsley or starts by Zach Eflin? Helsley – 8 , Eflin – 1. Both of these answers make me sad. (84% answered correctly)

OPS+ for Pete Alonso or Kyle Schwarber? Alonso – 149 , Schwarber – 128. We love you, Pete! (51.4%)

Colton Cowser K% or Cedric Mullins stolen bases? Cowser – 30.9% , Mullins – 21. Cowser struck out at the rate we pretty much expected. Mullins had a poor year on the basepaths. He stole 21 bases and was caught 10 times. (81.2%)

Taylor Ward bWAR or Trevor Rogers ERA? Rogers – 4.03 , Ward – 2.7. Rogers's number was higher than I expected and Ward's was about what I expected. (47.2%)

Chris Bassitt HR allowed or Coby Mayo HR hit? Mayo – 24 , Bassitt – 10. Next year we'll probably do an O/U on Mayo homers. (65.6%)

Dean Kremer BB or Blaze Alexander GS? Alexander – 74 , Kremer – 11. This one was lopsided by both Blaze's unexpectedly good play and Dean's unexpected trade. (73%)

OBP by Dylan Beavers or Ramón Laureano? Beavers – .307, Laureano – .286. Beavers essentially replaced Laureano in the lineup, and proved a better hitter this year. It was a low bar to cross; Laureano was not only bad at the plate, but he missed about 2/3 of the season with injury. (60.6%)

Playoff games at Camden Yards or Orioles with 30+ HR? 30+ homers – 1 (Pete!) ; Playoff games – 0. This one is a bummer (61%)

Gunnar Henderson SLG: .4995 – Under – .404 (21.6%)

Number of starting pitchers used: 12 ½ – Under – 10 (79.8%)

Jackson Holliday OPS: .7245 – Under – .640 (42.6%)

Kyle Bradish ERA: 2.755 – Over – 4.12 (74.5%)

This section stumped people as a whole. Look at those low percentages of right answers!

Will Jordan Westburg play a Major League game in 2026? No (27.7%)

Will Samuel Basallo make >50 starts at catcher? Yes (69.1%)

Will Adley Rutschman finish with at least 2 bWAR? No – 1.9 (6%)

Will the team ERA be under 4.00? No – 4.08 (41.1%)

Will Ryan Mountcastle be in the organization on Sept 27th? Yes (19.5%)

Who will make the second-most starts at first base? Alonso – 142, Mayo – 13 , Basallo – 4, Mountcastle – 2 (17.7%)

Which pitcher listed will make the most starts? Brandon Young – 28 , Trey Gibson – 8, Cade Povich – 7, Albert Suarez – 0. Young will no longer be lumped in with this tier of pitcher. (8.2%)

Which of the following prospects will have the most stolen bases in the minors? Enrique Bradfield – 44 , Aron Estrada – 8, Vance Honeycutt – 38, Nate George – 15. Estrada's steals went down as his power went up. George only played 20 games and still had 15 steals. (71.3%)

Against which AL East team will the Orioles have the most wins? Rays 8 , Jays – 7, Red Sox – 4, Yankees – 3. The Orioles had a winning record against the team with the most wins in the AL. Baseball is funny. (59.6%)

Which relief pitcher will have the most losses? Helsley – 4 , Wells – 2, Akin – , Cano – 3, Somebody else (Wolfram) – 4 (33.7%). If you chose Helsley or Wolfram, you got the points. Considering he missed so much time with injury, how did Helsley end up leading this category?

For the first time in contest history, we included questions about yearly awards, which are not announced until after the postseason. This was a mistake on our part, because the Orioles are not getting any awards. The questions are on the spreadsheet linked at the top of the page but have no scores. IF someone ends up winning (lol!) I'll come back and issue an addendum.

Thank you to everyone who played this year! I hope you had fun and we'll see you in the spring for the 2027 contest.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns offers 2028 four-star safety recruit Antwaun Adams
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns have offered 2028 four-star safety Antwaun Adams from Baylor High School in Chattanooga, Tennessee.
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns are looking to add to four-star quarterback Neimann Lawrence in the 2028 cycle. Four-star safety Antwaun Adams has nearly 30 offers from schools such as Alabama, Georgia, Oregon, Notre Dame, LSU, Ole Miss , Indiana, Florida State , Florida, and more.

Adams has now been extended an offer from Texas. He announced it social media.

"#AGTG blessed to receive an offer from Texas Longhorns ! 🤘🏾," said Adams.

Adams played a South Pike High School as a sophomore in Magnolia, Mississippi. He racked up 25 tackles (all solo), two tackles for loss, three interceptions (two return touchdowns), and one pass breakup. Adams also contributed as a wide receiver with 25 receptions for 466 yards and six touchdowns. He transferred to Baylor High School in Chattanooga, Tennessee for his junior campaign.

247Sports composite rankings have Adams listed as the No. 98 overall player and the No. 10 safety in the nation. The 6-foot-1, 185-pounder is the No. 4 prospect in the state of Tennessee as well.
